stories.title: Union Minister Shivraj stuck in Lucknow traffic jam:Leaves without attending wedding of senior BJP leader's daughter
stories.summary: Lucknow's traffic system has once again caused embarrassment. Union Agriculture Minister and former Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh Shivraj Singh Chouhan got stuck in such a traffic jam in the capital on Monday that he returned without attending the wedding ceremony. The return of this senior BJP leader in this manner is now bothering government and organization leaders. BJP MLC and BJP in-charge of Madhya Pradesh Mahendra Singh's daughter's wedding was on Monday at Janeshwar Mishra Park. In another section of Janeshwar Mishra Park itself, the wedding of state government minister Dinesh Pratap Singh's niece was also taking place. To attend the weddings at the homes of two senior leaders, CM Yogi Adityanath, Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, several ministers of the central government, national and state office bearers of BJP, ministers of the state government, several senior office bearers of RSS, MLAs, MPs and officials had arrived. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan also came to the wedding ceremony to bless the bride and groom. State government PWD Minister of State Brajesh Singh was assigned to Shivraj's protocol. Brajesh Singh reached Janeshwar Mishra Park with Shivraj Singh. Shivraj Singh attended the wedding of Dinesh Pratap Singh's niece and blessed the bride and groom and also gave them a gift. But ahead of that, his convoy got stuck in a traffic jam. Even after considerable effort, the jam did not clear, and due to being stuck in the jam, there was a possibility of Shivraj Singh missing his flight. Due to the heavy traffic jam, Shivraj Singh Chouhan handed over his gift to Brajesh Singh in an annoyed tone. He returned without attending the wedding ceremony. Brajesh Singh reached the stage and informed Mahendra Singh about this, and also presented the gift given by Shivraj Singh.

stories.title: Nuclear Medicine doctor at Lucknow cancer institute resigns:28 doctors leave in 5 years; complaints of low salaries
stories.summary: Kalyan Singh Super Speciality Cancer Institute has suffered another setback. Dr. Sonam Suman from the Nuclear Medicine Department of the institute has resigned. However, the clear reason for leaving the institute has not been mentioned in the resignation. Officials say that despite being a super speciality institute, the salary being given is that of a State Medical College. Whereas some doctors in the institute are being paid salaries equivalent to KGMU, PGI. The resignation of the woman doctor has dealt a blow to the operation of PET CT and other machines in the Nuclear Medicine Department. 400 patients are coming to the OPD of the Cancer Institute daily. There are approximately 300 beds. Most beds remain occupied all the time. 40 to 50 patients are being admitted daily in the emergency. Due to salary discrepancies and other mismanagement, 28 specialist doctors have left their jobs in the past five years. More than 60 nursing staff and about a dozen technicians and employees have bid farewell to the Cancer Institute. Not even a single doctor in these departments The institute does not have a single doctor in four departments. These include important departments such as Radio Diagnosis, Medical Oncology, Plastic Surgery, and Nuclear Medicine. Cancer patients are suffering the consequences of this. Patients are unable to get tests related to the Nuclear Medicine department done. Patients have to travel a distance of 20 to 25 kilometers. One Institute, Two Pay Scales Two types of pay scales are being provided to doctors at the Cancer Institute. About 24 doctors are being provided salary and allowances similar to SGPGI and KGMU. The remaining 10 doctors are being provided salary and allowances similar to State Medical College. Nursing, paramedical, and other category employees are being provided salaries similar to State Medical College. This has caused resentment among doctors and employees.

stories.title: Fine on beard and long hair at Lucknow's Lohia Institute:₹2,000 fine for taking leave without informing; ₹500 fine for sleeping or smoking
stories.summary: A major controversy has erupted over new rules issued for outsourced employees at Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences in Lucknow. According to the order issued by the agency, male employees will be fined Rs 200 for keeping a beard or long hair. Female employees will also have to pay a fine of Rs 200 for not keeping their hair in a bun or the prescribed hairstyle. Outsourcing Company Issues Order It is being reported that around 4000 outsourced employees are working in the institute. The agency's camp manager has issued this order on the instructions of the institute administration. Under this, a fine of Rs 100 has been fixed for not wearing an ID card or nameplate during duty and Rs 200 per day for not wearing the prescribed uniform. A fine of 500 rupees will be imposed for being absent from duty without notice or leaving the workplace. A penalty of up to 2000 rupees may have to be paid for taking leave or remaining absent without prior notice. A fine of 500 rupees has also been fixed for being found sleeping, smoking, or consuming alcohol during duty. The order also states that in cases of corrupt conduct, use of improper methods, or collusion with officials, an FIR will be filed along with termination of service if found guilty. Employees allege that such strict and unusual rules are not implemented in other institutions of the state. They have expressed opposition, calling this order impractical. The system will not apply to regular employees According to the aggrieved outsourcing employees, outsourcing companies are working on the instructions of the institution administration. Such orders have been issued to put pressure on outsourcing employees, whereas this order is not being applied to regular employees deployed in the institution, whose number is approximately 1000.

stories.title: 'We will conduct Rath Yatra for Hindu Rashtra':Dhirendra Shastri's Hanumant Katha in Prayagraj; says, 'Lenskart should open store in Lahore'
stories.summary: Today is the second day of Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, the Peethadhishwar of Bageshwar Dham's Hanumant Katha in Prayagraj. On the first day, he said that, ‘India will become a Hindu nation. Efforts are ongoing for that. Regarding the resolve for a Hindu nation, we will conduct a chariot procession this year. We will make the announcement on July 4th and provide complete information about the chariot procession.’ He said, ‘Those who have a problem with tilak, chandan, worship, Ram, Shyam, Hanuman, Baba Bageshwar, should quietly slip away to Lahore through the narrow lane. Reform yourselves, otherwise Indian law will reform you. UP police is famous anyway. Vehicles do get overturned.’ It's very hot here, from today the Katha will start at 5 o'clock Dhirendra Shastri said, 'The world's biggest Mahakumbh was held in Prayag. This is the land of Sanatan. Whatever you may be at your homes, but keep this thought in your hearts - we are Hindus, we are Sanatani. We have chosen Sundar Kand. We will narrate the Katha for three days.' 'It's very hot here, it's difficult for you to come during the day. That's why we decided to start the Katha at 4-5 o'clock. Otherwise, you might come to listen to the Katha and attain moksha, it's very difficult brother.' Gave reply to Bareilly's Maulana Shastri said, ‘One day, Rudra Abhishek will definitely be performed at Gyanvapi. The stain that exists next to Kashi Vishwanath Ji will be removed. We want crowds in temples, storms on the streets. We want a Hindustan filled with Ram Rajya. I have complete faith in the judiciary.’ On the question of opposition from a Maulana in Bareilly, Dhirendra Shastri said, 'It's a game of time. People worth two paise start selling for crores.' One day the saffron flag will also fly over Gyanvapi Dhirendra Shastri said that just as the Ram Temple was built, similarly one day the saffron flag will also fly over Gyanvapi. He reached Bamrauli Airport by helicopter on Tuesday afternoon. From here he traveled by car to Karela Bagh, then by steamer in the Yamuna to Arail Selfie Point. Upon his arrival, devotees raised slogans hailing Bageshwar Baba. Shastri said, ‘Lenskart should open a company in Lahore’ Dhirendra Shastri said, 'Lenskart company has imposed a ban on its workers that no one can come wearing a tilak. Cannot come wearing a mangalsutra, wearing sindoor. You open your company in Lahore. Why are you dying in India. Is India your uncle's? Yes, India is our father's.' 'Those who have a problem with tilak, chandan, vandan, Ram, Shyam, Hanuman, Baba Bageshwar, should slip away to Lahore through a narrow lane. We will also tell the Lenskart people, you have gone wrong. Correct yourself, otherwise Indian law also corrects.' 'I say to Hindus, today they have pointed fingers at your mangalsutra and tilak. If we Hindus do not unite, tomorrow they will point fingers at your community, Sanatan and children. Tomorrow they will also point fingers at our Gita and Ramayana.' However, two days ago, eyewear retailer company Lenskart publicly apologized after heavy opposition on social media. Apart from this, they have now issued a new and transparent 'in-store style guide', which gives employees complete permission to wear their religious and cultural symbols at the workplace. 13,000 square feet pandal on Yamuna banks A grand pandal has been constructed in 13 thousand square meters at the Katha venue located on the Yamuna riverbank. The Katha which started today on April 21 will conclude on April 23. On the first day, around 20-22 thousand devotees reached the pandal. Arrangements for the Katha have been made in an area of approximately six acres. 8 entry gates have been constructed in the pandal for devotees to enter and exit. 3000 police personnel, 500 CCTVs and drones have been deployed for surveillance. Amidst the huge crowd that came to listen to Dhirendra Shastri's Katha, one devotee arrived in a wheelchair. BJP Leader Organized the Katha Event The host of the Hanumant Katha is BJP leader Dr. Uday Pratap Singh, a resident of Prayagraj. He is the Director of Harinarayan Group of Colleges. He has a total of five colleges. Apart from this, he owns a rice mill. His father had a factory in Mirpur. Later, Uday Pratap started doing property business. Dr. Uday Pratap Singh has met Home Minister Amit Shah several times. He is also close to Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya. He has organized many events before this as well. These have included Bollywood actress and MP Kangana Ranaut, cricketer Suresh Raina, Bhojpuri actress Akshara Singh, singer Hansraj Raghuwanshi, and many other film artists. 6400 Square Feet Grand Stage, VVIP Gallery in Front For the katha (religious discourse), a stage approximately 100 feet long and 64 feet wide, totaling 6400 square feet, has been constructed. Behind the stage, there are 4 VVIP rooms. In front of the stage, a VVIP gallery of approximately 3000 square feet has been built where sofas have been placed. Here, seating arrangements have been made for more than 200 VVIPs. Behind this, chairs have been arranged for 500 VIPs. LED Screens, 250 Fans and VVIP Rooms in the Pandal To give devotees the experience of the katha from every corner, 8 large LED screens have been installed in the middle and back area of the pandal. More than 250 fans have been installed to provide relief from the heat. 3000 Police Personnel, 8 ASPs and 21 DSPs Deployed Around 3000 police personnel will be deployed during the Hanumant Katha. This will include 8 Additional SPs and 21 Deputy SP level officers. The entire event venue has been divided into 8 zones and 21 sectors. Additionally, 10 fire tenders and fire brigade teams will also be present. Additional police force has also been called from nearby districts. Reserve force will be deployed for emergency situations. During the Hanumant Katha, around 500 CCTV cameras will keep watch at every corner. 24-hour surveillance will be maintained through master screens from the control room. 50-bed hospital and community kitchen for 40 thousand people daily During the Katha, there will be special focus on crowd management. Considering the severe heat, a temporary 50-bed hospital has been set up. Doctors and health workers will be deployed there. During the Katha, Bhandara (community meal) is being prepared for 40 thousand people daily, which will be distributed in different pandals. 8 Parking Areas, 350 Traffic Police Personnel Deployed To maintain smooth traffic arrangements during the Katha, eight parking locations have been created. Devotees will park their vehicles in these parking areas and then will have to walk to the main event venue. For traffic management, approximately 350 traffic police personnel have been deployed on duty, who have been on alert since Tuesday morning.

stories.title: 'I cannot forget the pain of a lifetime':One year after Pahalgam attack, victim Shubham Dwivedi's wife Aishanya says, 'No justice till terrorism is eradicated'
stories.summary: The Pahalgam terrorist attack occurred exactly one year ago today on April 22. Terrorists killed 26 people after asking their names and religion. 30-year-old Shubham Dwivedi from Kanpur was shot in the head in front of his wife Aishanya. Shubham and Aishanya had been married for just two months. Even one year after the terrorist attack, tears come to Aishanya's eyes when she remembers Shubham. She says she could neither celebrate their anniversary nor any festival. Shubham's father Sanjay Dwivedi has kept his son's photograph in his office, which he looks at before sitting on his chair. He also organizes a community feast in his village every month in Shubham's name. Aishanya and Shubham's father Sanjay Dwivedi had an exclusive conversation with Bhaskar. They shared their emotions. Aishanya said, ‘There can be no greater sorrow than when a son leaves the world in front of his parents. When someone who had been married for just two months has their husband killed by terrorists right in front of them, no one can forget that. Now this has become a lifelong pain.’ 'How happy we were, everything was destroyed' Aishanya becomes emotional remembering the entire incident. She says, ‘We had gone out for a trip on April 17 last year. Since that date this year, I have been constantly remembering those moments. I am looking at the pictures from that time. Looking at those pictures, it feels like how happy we were, but April 22 destroyed everything for me.’ 'The pain of a lifetime...I cannot forget' Aishanya says, 'When a 30-year-old son passes away in front of his parents, there can be no greater sorrow than that. When a life partner is snatched away in front of their spouse, when their husband is killed, no one can forget that. This is a lifelong trauma. There were 26 people with her husband, her husband was killed in front of the wives. This is the pain of an entire lifetime. I cannot forget this.' 'I don't understand whom to tell about the good work' Aishanya says, 'When you lose someone, every day becomes difficult. Whether it's a festival or an anniversary. We had been married for only two months. I didn't celebrate any anniversary with him, nor any festival. I remember him every moment. Whenever I do something good, I feel like sharing it, then I wonder who should I tell.' 'I am getting strength from my family itself' Aishanya says that, ‘If family is with you, that is the biggest strength. Along with my in-laws, I also got the support of my parents. Because of which we were able to bear all this. We became strong because of staying together. I am getting strength from my family itself.’ 'No second meeting with PM, CM had come' Aishanya says, 'There was no second meeting with PM Modi but the CM had come to our place. Then my father-in-law, Shubham's father, met the CM in June-July 2025. There were also conversations over the phone several times. There are attempts to meet the CM, but due to the Bengal elections, the meeting could not happen yet. But I have to meet him, I am trying.' 'Relief will come only when terrorism is completely eliminated' Aishanya says, ‘After Operation Sindoor, Operation Mahadev also took place, in which terrorist hideouts were first destroyed. In Operation Mahadev, those terrorists who had done this were eliminated. Information keeps coming that military operations continue to be conducted at other hideouts in Kashmir as well. Both operations are a relief, but until terrorism is completely eliminated, full relief will not be achieved.’ 'Is your country first or religion?' Aishanya says, 'This is not just a terrorist attack, but a Hindu genocide. Because there, Hindus were targeted based on their religion, forced to recite the Kalma, and then killed. They were asked whether they were Hindu or Muslim. If Muslim, recite the Kalma, then they were targeted. Terrorism has no religion. Terrorists have a very disgusting mindset, they are not human. In our Puranas, there were demons, these are those same demons. Why are they only from one particular religious community, I don't have an answer to that. But this question must certainly be asked: is your country first or your religion?' 'Making efforts to preserve memories' Aishanya says that Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana has been in constant touch with our family. He also had a gate built in Shubham's ancestral village. When he came to lay its foundation stone, he said that they would also install a biopic of Shubham in the digital library of the Assembly. Every effort is being made to preserve Shubham's memories. We met him just two days ago. We keep talking on the phone as well. He is the one person who is constantly in touch with us. The tender for a park has been done, some technical matters are stuck. As soon as they are completed, work on the park will begin. There is no information about other things yet. Aishanya's response on the question of entering politics When asked about entering politics, Aishanya says, 'I am 28 years old right now, I have never thought about anything like that. But if the question is there, then I have always been involved in social work anyway. Now I don't have a life partner in my life, so I keep thinking about doing social work only.' 'What will happen ahead, I don't know, because whatever has happened in my life till now, I had never thought about that either. Two months after marriage, I lost everything in the attack, I had never thought about that either.' Father Sanjay says, ‘Never thought even in dreams that such an incident would happen’ We also spoke to Shubham's father Sanjay Dwivedi. Recalling those moments, he says, 'It had been only two months since his son's wedding. Both families had happily planned together for the children to go to Kashmir.' 'But never thought even in dreams that such an incident would happen with the family. After that, what happened, there can be no greater sorrow than this for us and the family. Every day we remember him, but as God keeps you, you have to remain that way.' 'As that date is approaching, the memory of that accident and that day is becoming fresh. On April 22, a program is also being organized in Kanpur to pay tribute to Shubham. The courage, cooperation and strength that the people of Kanpur have given us has helped us bear that grief.' It was difficult to console Shubham's mother after the accident Sanjay Dwivedi says that on February 26, Shubham's birthday, and on February 12, the day he got married, he was missed very much. 'The biggest difficulty was in consoling Shubham's mother. We cannot take anyone away from Shubham's memory, but still somehow we managed to console them.' Sanjay says, 'On the 22nd of every month, we organize a feast in our village in Shubham's name, so on that date it feels like how many months have passed since Shubham left us.' Operation Sindoor gave us satisfaction Sanjay Dwivedi says that ‘Assembly Speaker Satish Mahana is very close to our family. When I was coming from Kashmir with Shubham, the CM also called me. The government helped us a lot.’ 'The government conducted Operation Sindoor, which not only gave us satisfaction but also must have brought peace to Shubham's soul. I had made a demand to the PM that it was an attack on the country, in which 26 people were killed by terrorists. Therefore, we had demanded that martyr status be given. We are still making that demand.' 'During that time, leaders of several political parties had met and also put forward my demand. Even Rahul Gandhi had said that he would write a letter to the PM for this. As for Akhilesh Yadav, he did not come to meet, because he had said that we come from the upper caste, so he won't come. He only goes to Muslims and PDA people's places. He has no concern for us.' Terrorists shot tourists in the valley after asking their names Shubham Dwivedi (30) from Kanpur was shot dead in a terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir on April 22, 2025. Aishanya had told that she was sitting with Shubham at a restaurant in Baisaran valley. Around 2:15 PM, terrorists came and started firing indiscriminately. This created a chaotic situation there. A terrorist asked Shubham his name. As soon as he revealed his name, Shubham was shot in the head. Shubham fell to the ground and Aishanya fainted. 26 people were killed in the terrorist attack. After this, the Indian government launched Operation Sindoor against Pakistan.

stories.title: Temperatures rise to 44°C in UP:Heatwave alert in 35 districts, Prayagraj hottest; rain likely after 4 days of intense heat
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is experiencing intense heat. A heat wave alert has been issued for 35 districts today, Wednesday. The sun has shone brightly since morning, and strong winds are blowing. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) says there is no hope of relief from the heat for four days, until April 25th. The mercury could reach 45°C. However, rain is expected on April 26th. In the last 24 hours, temperatures in 30 districts across the state have exceeded 40°C. Prayagraj was the hottest, reaching 44.4°C during the day. Two hippos were seen frolicking underwater at the Gorakhpur Zoo. A tourist visiting the Taj Mahal in Agra fell unconscious. Five to six tourists fell ill. The intense heat has led to numerous fires across the state. A market in Ghaziabad caught fire amid the scorching sun, destroying 20 shops, including a restaurant. Buses also caught fire in Meerut and Lucknow. In Meerut, the bus was carrying about 50 passengers. However, everyone was able to safely evacuate before the fire spread. In view of the increasing heat and heatwave, the Basic Education Department has changed the opening hours of council schools. Now, all council schools in the state will open from 7:30 am to 1:30 pm. Classes will run from 7:30 am to 12:30 pm. After this, teachers and other staff will remain in the school until 1:30 pm to complete academic and administrative work. Visuals of the intense heat Heat wave warning in these 30 districts The 30 districts for which the Meteorological Department has issued a heat wave warning include Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, Lakhimpur Kheri, Sitapur, Bahraich, Shravasti, Balrampur, Gonda, Basti, Sant Kabir Nagar, Siddharthnagar, Maharajganj, Gorakhpur, Kushinagar, Deoria, Azamgarh, Mau, Ballia, Ghazipur, Jaunpur, Varanasi, Chandauli, Mirzapur, Sonbhadra, Prayagraj, Pratapgarh, Amethi, Ambedkar Nagar, Sultanpur, Ayodhya and surrounding areas. Meteorologists say that now the night temperature will also rise. Gradually the minimum temperature will reach 25 to 30°C. Avoid going out of the house during the afternoon. The Meteorological Department has urged people to be cautious about the heat. They have advised people to avoid prolonged exposure to the sun and to only venture outside during the day when absolutely necessary. They have also urged people to take special care of children and the elderly. The Meteorological Department has advised people to drink plenty of water. Wear light and loose clothing. Cover your head when leaving the house. Use a hat, scarf, or umbrella. Contact a doctor if you experience dizziness, headache, high fever, vomiting, or weakness. How will the weather be in the next 5 days? April 23 – Bright sunshine will prevail across the state. Humidity will increase due to reduced wind speed. April 24 – Eastern and western Uttar Pradesh will experience intense sunshine, with heat waves possible in some areas during the afternoon. April 25 – The weather will be dry with bright sunshine throughout the state. A heat wave will develop during the afternoon. April 26 – A heat wave alert has been issued for eastern and western Uttar Pradesh. The intense sun will increase humidity. April 27 – Rain and thundershowers are possible in western Uttar Pradesh, while eastern Uttar Pradesh will remain hot.

stories.title: 'Muslims who become saints are welcomed, so why oppose me?':Influencer turned Sadhvi Harsha Richhariya says, 'I will remain active on social media'
stories.summary: 'I am not Sita, that I should give an Agni Pariksha (trial by fire). The story that began with Mahakumbh 2025 is now ending. I faced opposition, character assassination and mental pressure. Therefore, now leaving the path of religion, I am returning to my old profession.' Social media influencer Harsha Richhariya said these things in a video on January 12, 2026. Just 3 months after this statement, on April 19, 2026, she took Sannyasa (renunciation) in Ujjain. She performed her own Pindadan and Shraddh. After this, she received a new name, Sadhvi Harshanand Giri. Bhaskar spoke with Harsha about the reason for taking Sannyasa and about her future plans. Read the full report. Harsha said, 'An inner voice came to take Sannyasa' Harsha was in Ujjain. We spoke to her on mobile. The first question asked was what was the reason behind taking Sannyasa? Harsha says, 'I had reached Mahakumbh for the first time as a Sadhvi. From what I felt there, the thought came that now Sannyasa can be taken.' 'From that very time my mind was wandering. After Mahakumbh, I became connected to Dharma. I understood everything related to Sanatan properly. In December 2025, my mind was firmly made up that now I should take Sannyasa. I listened to my inner voice and now have taken Sannyasa. No guru inspired me to do this.' 'Mother's condition deteriorated upon hearing about renunciation' We asked - What did your parents say when they heard about renunciation? She says, 'They were shocked. Why wouldn't they be. Every family would find it strange if their daughter talks about taking renunciation. They didn't agree. My mother was crying continuously. Her condition had worsened significantly. But, gradually they understood that I wasn't going to do anything wrong. Now mother is not with me, nor am I with her. Now I don't know what condition she is in. Perhaps she must have understood that ultimately renunciation is the truth.' Harsha says, 'Not teaching anything wrong on social media' We asked, 'Despite taking Sannyasa, will you continue giving spiritual messages on social media? She says- Tell me one thing, am I teaching anything wrong on social media...no, right? In today's date, big leaders and religious gurus are active on social media. Lakhs of people listen to and watch their messages. I don't think there's a need to distance myself from it. Through this, we can reach our message far and wide.' 'The reason for my troubles was none other than saints' We asked - Why did you say that on the path of dharma you only found character assassination? Harsha says, ‘I had never come so close to Sanatan Dharma before Mahakumbh. When I came, many sadhus and saints started opposing me.’ 'They started saying that a dancer-singer has been made a sanyasi, whereas where was I dancing and singing. I used to do anchoring. I had built my identity through that work. I never did anything wrong. Despite this, I was opposed.' 'There was a time when I became very troubled. The reason for my trouble was none other than the saints themselves. At that time, it came to my mind that when a Muslim person adopts Hinduism, people welcome them so much. But when a daughter of Hindu dharma came, even religious gurus started opposing. Seeing all this, my mind was disturbed.' 'The path of religion is not easy for girls' Do you think the path of religion is difficult for girls? Harsha says, 'Women are emotional. People take advantage of this. That's why the path of religion is a bit difficult for women. When a woman is not wrong, she breaks down quickly.' 'She starts thinking what sin have I committed that I am being targeted. To break a woman, people start character assassination. Because, they know that no matter how strong a girl is, when it comes to character, she will break.' 'Some saints also raised fingers at my character. They said many things, but I stood firm. What they were saying was their mentality. What I am doing is my decision.' On posting bridal look photos, she says, ‘Now everything is left behind’ We asked - You had shared your pictures in western clothes 4 days ago. Was that to remember for the last time? She says, 'There was a lot of pressure on me. I didn't want to tell anyone what I was going to do next. That's why 4 days ago I confused people by posting bridal look videos-photos. Those pictures were old. Just posted them that day. Now I have taken sannyasa. Everything is left behind.' 'Will work for the country and society' What are your future plans? Harsha says, 'What can I tell you now. I'll just say this much that now I will work openly for society, for the younger generation and for the country. This is not wrong work. Now if someone has a problem even with the right thing, then I can't do anything about it.'

stories.title: 'Blue drum' murder case accused Muskaan claims she was framed:Says, 'I was touring Shimla-Mussoorie with Sahil'; judge asks 32 questions in Meerut court
stories.summary: In the famous Saurabh Rajput murder case of Meerut, accused Muskaan-Sahil presented their side in the district court on Tuesday, 21 April. Judge Anupam Kumar asked both of them 32 questions. Both said - we are being falsely implicated in Saurabh Rajput's murder. In 29 questions, Muskaan-Sahil completely denied the allegations. However, they answered yes to visiting and staying together in Kasol-Mussoorie and Shimla after the murder. Both said in their answers that we went on a trip together, we also stayed, but we did not commit murder. What happened in court? In District Judge Anupam Kumar's court, proceedings under Section-313 took place in the Saurabh Rajput murder case. Murder accused Muskaan-Sahil presented their side one by one. District Judge Anupam Kumar first asked Sahil 32 questions. After this, Muskaan was called to the witness box. Muskaan was also asked the same 32 questions. Both their statements were recorded. After this, Muskaan-Sahil were sent to the district jail. 7 major questions asked to Sahil Question: You are accused of murdering Muskaan's husband Saurabh Rajput. What do you have to say? Answer: This accusation is completely false, I am innocent. Question: Why has a case been filed against you? Answer: I don't know why this murder charge has been put on me? I am being falsely implicated. I had just gone for a stroll, that's why they are framing me. Question: Do you have anything to say in your defense or in your favor? Answer: No, nothing more to say. I'll just say that I have been wrongly implicated. Question: Hotel owners in Shimla, Kasol, Mussoorie say that you stayed in hotels here? Answer: Yes, that is correct. Question: Saurabh's friends say that they saw you going to Muskaan's house? Answer: This is completely false. I did not go to her house. Question: The drum seller, knife, cutter, sand sellers said that you purchased these items from them? Answer: All these allegations are completely false. I did not purchase any items. Question: Do you have anything to say in your defense, anything to present? Answer: Yes, I want to present my side. I want to give my defense. Sahil says, ‘I will present witnesses in court to prove my innocence’ When the judge asked Sahil in court if he wanted to say anything in his defense? To this, Sahil said in strong words, ‘I am innocent, I am being framed. I want to prove my innocence. To prove my innocence, I want to present my witness.’ The next date in the case is set for 28 April. Then Sahil's lawyer Rekha Jain will present witnesses and evidence on his behalf. ‘I was in Delhi on the night of the murder’ Sahil presented his side saying that on the night of Saurabh's murder, he was not in Meerut but in Delhi. It is believed that on April 28, Sahil will strongly present this point to prove his innocence that on the night of Saurabh's murder, he was in Delhi. Muskaan said, 'Case filed due to property dispute' When Muskaan was asked why a case was filed against you for your husband Saurabh Rajput's murder? How are you an accused? On this, Muskaan clearly said that the case was filed due to a property dispute. 7 major questions asked to Muskaan Question: You are accused of murdering your husband Saurabh Rajput, what do you say? Answer: This accusation is completely false, I am innocent. Question: Why was a case filed against you? Answer: I have been wrongly implicated in the case due to a property dispute. Question: Do you want to say anything in your defense or on your behalf? Answer: No, nothing more to say. I will just say that I have been wrongly implicated. Question: Hotel owners in Shimla, Kasol, Mussoorie say that you stayed there with Sahil Shukla? Answer: Yes, that's correct. I had gone for a trip and stayed there. Question: Saurabh's friends say that they saw Sahil coming and going to your house? Answer: Wrong and false. That did not happen. Question: The drum seller, knife, cutter, sand-cement sellers said that you purchased these items from them? Answer: All these allegations are completely false. Question: A doctor residing in Brahmpuri alleges that he prescribed a medicine to you on a prescription? Answer: This is wrong and baseless. Nothing like that happened. Sahil saw Muskaan's daughter Radha for the first time Sahil-Muskaan came to court together on 21 April, 2026, after 18 March, 2025. 13 months ago, both were sent to jail after being presented in the same court. Since then, both were having online hearings. On 21 April, both remained together for about one and a half hours. First, both were kept seated in the police van, where Sahil saw the face of Muskaan's daughter Radha for the first time. After this, both were presented in court. Both remained there together for 46 minutes. However, both could not talk to each other in the courtroom. The murder case came to light on 17 March, 2025 In Meerut's Brahmpuri area, on 3 March, Saurabh was murdered by his wife Muskaan along with her lover Sahil Rajput. After this, the body was cut into 3 pieces, put in a drum, and sealed with a mixture of cement and sand. The case was uncovered on 17 March. On 18 March, Muskaan and Sahil were sent to jail. Testimony of 22 witnesses completed In the Merchant Navy Officer Saurabh murder case, statements of 22 witnesses have been recorded so far. After these testimonies, the prosecution's evidence has been closed. Now the process under Section 313 will begin in court. After this, final arguments will take place and then the court will pronounce its verdict. Know the complete case Muskaan-Sahil stayed in the lobby all night with the body Muskaan of the blue drum case reached court with daughter in her lap, arrived in police van with lover Sahil after 13 months in jail In the much-discussed Saurabh murder case of Meerut, accused Muskaan and her lover Sahil were presented in court on Tuesday. Both were brought from jail to court amid heavy security. Both remained in court for about 46 minutes. During this time, the judge questioned Sahil for 20 minutes and Muskaan for 16 minutes. After this, the police took both back to jail in the same manner they had brought them to court.

stories.title: Lover marries bride in 'mandap' meant for groom:UP man reveals five-year relationship to groom’s family hours before marriage
stories.summary: A police sub-inspector’s wedding took a dramatic and unexpected turn when it was called off just hours before the wedding procession’s departure, after the bride’s long-time lover revealed their relationship to the groom’s family. The lover later married the woman at the same wedding venue. The incident took place in the Duboulia police station area. Marriage fixed with Sub-Inspector, preparations complete The bride was set to marry John Major, a sub-inspector in the Uttar Pradesh Police, currently posted in Lucknow. His father, Dharmraj Chaudhary, is a principal at a government inter college in Uttarakhand. The wedding was scheduled for 20 April, and both families had completed all arrangements. Invitations had been distributed, guests had arrived, and pre-wedding rituals were underway at the groom’s residence. Lover arrives, discloses relationship On Monday, 20 April morning, just hours before the wedding procession was to depart, Sarvesh Singh, a property dealer from the Mehndawal area, arrived at the groom’s house around 11:30 am. He informed the groom’s family that he had been in a relationship with the bride for the past five years. He also warned them against proceeding with the wedding, saying he would disclose the relationship publicly if the marriage went ahead. Groom’s family calls off wedding After hearing him out, the groom’s father contacted the bride’s family to verify the claims. Upon confirmation, the groom’s family decided to call off the wedding and informed the bride’s side that the procession would not arrive. Lover marries bride in same venue The sudden cancellation caused panic at the bride’s home, where all arrangements had already been made. Soon after, Sarvesh Singh reached the bride’s house, spoke to her family, and convinced them to agree to the marriage. Later that night, he arrived as the groom with a Baraat and married his partner in the same wedding venue.

stories.title: 5 killed after being run over by train in Prayagraj:Were standing below after getting down from coach; hit by 2 trains
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, 5 people died after being hit by a train around 7:30 PM on Wednesday evening. Upon receiving information, police and railway teams reached the spot and took possession of the bodies, sending them for post-mortem. According to the police, efforts are being made to identify the deceased. The accident occurred at Pachdeora Halt in the Karchhana area. Passengers had got down from the train at a halt station Akash (19), son of Giriraj and a resident of Prithvipur village under Khairgarh police station in Firozabad, was travelling to attend a wedding at a relative’s house in Kolkata. Ajay, son of Munna Pasi and a resident of Kolkata, was also with him. Near Pachdevara, a man fell from the same train, after which the emergency chain was pulled and the train stopped. All the passengers got down to relieve themselves. At that moment, the Kalka Mail sounded its horn and people started moving back towards the train. Meanwhile, the Purushottam Express, coming from the Mirzapur side, hit five people, killing all of them. Two of the deceased have been identified as Akash Kumar from Firozabad and Sunil Kumar from Mirzapur. Three bodies remain unidentified. As soon as the information was received, the Karchana police, ACP Sunil Kumar Singh, GRP and railway officials reached the spot. See 3 pictures Passengers had alighted from the train at Halt station A train stopped for a while near Pachdeora Halt. A passenger got down and went to the other track to use the toilet. Just then, the Kalka Mail arrived, and the young man died on the spot after being hit by it. Seeing this incident, passengers on the train raised an alarm. The deceased's family members got down in a panic, and then another train also arrived, and all three were hit by it. They also died on the spot in this accident. After the incident, another person is reported missing. It is suspected that he was also hit by the train, although this has not been officially confirmed yet. Upon receiving the information, police from Karchhana police station, ACP Sunil Kumar Singh, GRP, and railway officials reached the spot.

stories.title: UP to have 120 Lok Sabha seats in next election:Currently 80 seats; change after Delimitation Commission is formed
stories.summary: The special session of Parliament in New Delhi is starting tomorrow (Thursday). The government is going to form a Delimitation Commission and introduce the 131st Constitution Amendment Bill. If both these bills are passed by a two-thirds majority in the House, then the picture of UP regarding the 2029 Lok Sabha elections will also become clear. UP's seats in the Lok Sabha can be increased from 80 to 120. Meanwhile, the Assembly seats can increase from 403 to 550-600. The number of Lok Sabha seats in UP has been increased from time to time based on the recommendations of the Delimitation Commission. What is the 131st Constitution Amendment? The Constitution Amendment Bill proposes to increase the Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850. Of these, a maximum of 815 seats will be for states and 35 for Union Territories. A Delimitation Commission will be formed to determine the number of seats. The commission will also decide how many seats each state will have. According to sources, the 2011 census will be considered the basis for the new delimitation. The distribution of seats will be determined based on population. In 2011, Uttar Pradesh's population was 16% of the country's total population. In this regard, if the Lok Sabha has 835 seats for states, then based on population, UP's seats could increase from 80 to 120-130. 40 seats will be reserved for women If the Lok Sabha seats in UP reach 120 after the new delimitation, then 33% of those seats will be reserved for women. This means only women MPs will be elected on 40 seats. This will also give an opportunity to women workers of political parties to go to Parliament. Assembly Seats Will Increase to 600 Experts believe that the current number of UP Assembly seats is based on the 1971 census. The population has increased significantly in the last 55 years. In 2026, the estimated population of UP has been assessed at 24.82 crore. In five and a half decades, migration from villages to cities has also been very high. The number of cities has increased. In UP, on average, there are more than 4 lakh voters in one assembly constituency. However, in the recently conducted Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter list, the number of voters has decreased. Still, the number of voters in UP's assembly constituencies is higher than in other states. If the formula of increasing seats according to population and reducing the burden of voters in existing assembly constituencies is implemented, the assembly seats here will increase to 550 to 600. Among these, 33% of seats (from 181 to 198) will be reserved for women. Assembly election seats could increase from 2032 In 2027, the assembly elections will be held on 403 seats only, but in the 2032 assembly elections, the number of seats will increase. Experts believe that if One Nation-One Election is implemented, the assembly seats in UP will increase even before 2032. Currently 12% Women MLAs in the Assembly Currently, there are 51 women MLAs in the UP Assembly compared to 403 seats. Among these, there are 30 from BJP, 15 from Samajwadi Party, 4 from Apna Dal (S), one from RLD, and one woman MLA from Congress. Assembly constituencies will be within the ambit of a single Lok Sabha constituency After the new delimitation, a major problem of political parties will be resolved. There are many Lok Sabha constituencies in UP whose assembly constituencies are within the boundaries of more than one district. In the new delimitation, it will be ensured that all assembly constituencies under a Lok Sabha constituency are within the boundaries of a single district. An assembly constituency will also not be divided between two Lok Sabha constituencies.

stories.title: Massive fire guts over 50 huts in Lucknow:LPG cylinders explode; man claims 4 children charred to death
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in the Vikasnagar area of Lucknow on Wednesday evening around 5:30 pm, destroying over 50 slum huts and triggering explosions of more than 30 LPG cylinders. The flames were so intense that they were visible from nearly 10 kilometres away. As the fire spread rapidly, around 20 nearby houses were evacuated as a precaution. Fire brought under control after 3 hours Around 20 fire brigade vehicles were deployed to control the blaze, which was finally brought under control after nearly three hours. Electricity supply in the area was cut off during the firefighting operation to prevent further hazards. A local resident claimed that his four children were burnt alive in the fire, though official confirmation is awaited. Several families lost all their belongings as their huts were reduced to ashes. Those affected were seen wailing in distress as they watched their homes burn down. Allegations of deliberate fire Some residents alleged that the fire may have been deliberately set, though authorities have not confirmed this. An investigation into the cause of the fire is underway. CM orders swift action Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took cognisance of the incident and directed officials to immediately reach the spot and oversee relief efforts. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak also visited the site and instructed authorities to expedite rescue and relief operations.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts are women; SC continues hearing in Sabarimala women entry case on Day 4 more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Sabarimala women entry case hearing on Day 4: Adv Singhvi says court can’t rule on religious beliefs A hearing is underway in the Supreme Court of India concerning the entry of women into the Sabarimala Temple. 2. Parents plan to sell their newborn fails: Grandmother rescues child; mother had struck a deal with a businessman for 2.5 lakhs In Agra, a mother made a deal to sell her two-day-old newborn baby. The price of the baby was fixed at Rs 2.5 lakh. A businessman even reached the hospital to take the baby, but the grandmother and aunt got wind of it. 3. Woman remains unidentified 5 days after her dead body recovery: Post-mortem report shows 17 injury marks The post-mortem report of the unidentified woman's body found by the roadside in the Kakori area has arrived. The report shows two severe injury marks on the front and back of the woman's head, while about 15 injuries were found on other parts of the body. 4. 'Har ghar bhagwa chhaega, Ram Rajya aaega', says BJP's Suvendu Adhikari Suvendu Adhikari, Leader of the Opposition in West Bengal and BJP candidate from Nandigram and Bhabanipur, said that “the public is ready”. He raised a slogan while campaigning, ‘Har ghar bhagwa chhaega, Ram Rajya aaega’. 5. Women DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts:33% posting plan before 2027 polls Efforts are underway in Uttar Pradesh to increase women’s participation in governance, with the first impact likely to be seen in district-level administration. 6. 4-year-old girl shows no fear of water: Swims 900 metres across the Yamuna River in 21 minutes In Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh, 4-year-old Satya Bharti from the Mahewa West area has achieved a feat that even seasoned swimmers often find challenging. She swam across the Yamuna river in just 21 minutes and 28 seconds. 7. Dalal Street cheers Modi-Trump call over Hormuz Strait trade Following the conversation between US President Donald Trump and his India counterpart PM Modi, the Indian benchmark indices advanced in early deals on Wednesday, 15 April, 2026. Sensex soared 1,300 points at opening. 8. Misleading video sparks FIR on 2 RJD women spokespersons After two days of unrest, factories in Noida reopened on Wednesday, with the situation returning to normal. Heavy security has been deployed, with surveillance through CCTV cameras and drones. 9. 3 years after Atiq’s killing, wife Shaista is still missing:2 other family members are absconding Three years on, the UP Police has failed to trace Atiq Ahmed’s wife, Shaista Parveen. Raids were conducted across nine states, with support from ATS and RAF teams, but she remains untraceable. 10. India's wholesale inflation rises for the 5th month in a row to 3.88% Wholesale prices of goods in India have gone up again in March 2025, increasing by 3.88%, the government data showed. This marks the fifth month in a row that prices have climbed.

stories.title: Woman climbs water tank for boyfriend, threatens to end life:Family conducts garland ceremony in Gorakhpur; wedding was fixed elsewhere on April 21
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, an 18-year-old girl climbed a 70-foot-high water tank on Tuesday evening, demanding to marry her boyfriend and threatening to end her life. She shouted from the top, asking people to call her boyfriend and warned that she would kill herself if anyone tried to stop her. Soon, a large crowd gathered at the spot and tried to convince her to come down, but she refused. Police also reached the scene after getting information, but their efforts failed to calm her. After nearly two hours, her boyfriend was brought there and both families agreed to the marriage. Only then did the girl come down safely. Later, the couple exchanged garlands and got married on the spot. After the ceremony, the girl was sent to the boy’s house. The incident took place in Mahavir Chhapra village under Belipar police station area. The couple had been in a relationship for four years, but the girl’s family had fixed her marriage elsewhere, scheduled for April 21. Met during college studies The girl said - she was studying intermediate, and during that time, she met a young man (19) from the same village. In 2022, we first became friends, and then gradually fell in love with each other. We have been in a relationship for four years. My family was not ready for the marriage. They fixed my marriage with another boy. The wedding procession was due to arrive on April 21st. I refused the marriage, but my family did not agree. They also stopped me from leaving the house. I tried to convince my parents, but they didn't agree. On April 14, Tuesday, at 3 PM, I reached near the water tank of the Jal Jeevan Mission located in Jotbagahi village. I thought that if my family didn't agree today, I would jump and end my life. People bowed to the girl's stubbornness, pressured the family to agree Villagers said that many attempts were made to get the girl down, but she did not agree. The police also tried to explain. Seeing her stubbornness, we talked to her family. Both families were called. The police spoke to both families and then they agreed to the marriage. After the family agreed, the girl was brought down. The varmala ceremony was arranged right there. And the two were married in front of everyone. After this, the girl was sent with the boy. After the marriage, the young woman was sent with her husband SP South Dinesh Puri said - The young woman was safely brought down. She was handed over to her family. Then, on the spot, both families were talked to and consent for the marriage was obtained. After this, the young woman was married. After the varmala ceremony, the girl was sent with her boy.

stories.title: Big setback for Baahubali Dhananjay, Abhay Singh acquitted:Varanasi court verdict in 24-year-old Taksal case, firing allegation involved
stories.summary: Strongman Dhananjay Singh has suffered a setback in the 24-year-old Taksal Cinema incident of Varanasi. The MP-MLA Court on Wednesday acquitted all 6 accused, including Abhay Singh and Mirzapur MLC Vineet Singh. Dhananjay had alleged that Abhay and Vineet Singh, along with 4-5 associates, had indiscriminately fired upon his convoy. In this, he, his gunner, and driver were injured. On April 13, Special Judge (MP-MLA Court) Yajuvendra Vikram Singh had reserved the verdict. Security was beefed up in and around the court premises in view of the verdict. More than 350 policemen, including 2 IPS officers and 3 ACPs, were deployed. One company of PAC (Provincial Armed Constabulary) was also called. Meanwhile, on Tuesday night, before the judgment, Dhananjay Singh bowed his head at Baba Vishwanath Temple and performed Rudrabhishek. He also offered prayers at the Kalbhairav Temple. He had said - 'We will definitely get justice.' Know the full story 1- Abhay got Dhananjay a hostel by calling him his maternal aunt's son According to Abhay Singh, Dhananjay Singh, who graduated from Karra College in Jaunpur in 1992, was first introduced by Dharmendra Singh, the president of Tilakdhari Singh College. It was the day of Dussehra. It was then that he said Dhananjay was also going to Lucknow to study, and asked to help him. According to Abhay Singh, Dhananjay's admission was arranged by his close friend Piyush Singh. Piyush was also studying at Lucknow University. However, Dhananjay Singh has himself narrated the story of his admission. According to him, admission was then through an entrance exam. He had passed the entrance test in both Prayagraj and Lucknow universities, but he decided to take admission in Lucknow University. At Lucknow University, Abhay Singh was one year senior to Dhananjay Singh in studies. He was already living in room number 51 in the hostel. He lied to the hostel warden that Dhananjay was his aunt's son. After this, Dhananjay Singh was allotted room number 18 on the lower floor of Abhay Singh's hostel. 2- The friendship of the three was famous in the university Arun Upadhyay, also from Jaunpur, was studying at Lucknow University. He was active in student politics. Due to their connection with Jaunpur, Abhay and Dhananjay were friends with him. According to Abhay Singh, his dream was to qualify for UPSC. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh says that he had only two dreams from the beginning: first, to join the army, and second, to enter politics after retirement. This trio became famous on the university campus. The three were seen together in protests against the Mandal agitation. At that time, Lucknow University had dominance across the entire state. Arun Upadhyay was preparing for the General Secretary election. Their friendship lasted until 2002. After this, their relationship started to sour. In 2002, Dhananjay Singh was subjected to a deadly attack in Banaras. Dhananjay Singh filed an FIR, naming his close friend Abhay Singh as the accused. 3- How Both Got the Title of Strongman Former Jaunpur MP Dhananjay Singh of Jaunpur and Abhay Singh, MLA from Goshainganj, Ayodhya, are known as strongman leaders in politics. Dhananjay Singh claimed in an interview with Dainik Bhaskar that after meeting Abhay Singh, he also became an accused in every one of Abhay Singh's cases. Later, when he became active in politics, cases kept piling up due to political reasons. On the other hand, Abhay Singh claims that before Arun Upadhyay's student elections, only one assault case was registered against him. After this, all other cases were registered. Many cases were registered even without any crime. In many, he was also made an accused in Dhananjay Singh's crimes. 4- In 1996, Abhay went to jail, and Dhananjay absconded In 1996, Hemant Singh was murdered. At that time, the then SSP Surya Kumar Shukla in Lucknow made both Abhay and Dhananjay accused. However, Abhay Singh claims that both of them were falsely implicated in this case. On January 11, 1996, Abhay Singh went to jail in a case registered for attempted murder and remained there for 4 and a half years. Dhananjay Singh remained absconding till February 1999. 5- Dispute in jail, both went their separate ways After Dhananjay surrendered in February 1999, he met Abhay in jail. There, a dispute arose between the two over old incidents, tender money, and the murders of Santosh and Abhishek. From there, both went their separate ways. In 2000, Abhay was released on bail. He met Naseemuddin Siddiqui in jail. Through him, Abhay Singh got his first MLA ticket from BSP in 2002. But he lost. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh contested the Rari assembly election as an independent in 2002 and won. On October 4, 2002, Dhananjay Singh's convoy was attacked. Dhananjay filed a case against Abhay, and since then, their paths diverged. Whenever they get a chance, they keep showering accusations on each other. When Dhananjay's close associates Alok Singh and Manish Singh Tata were caught in the codeine cough syrup case, Abhay had then taunted him by calling him 'Codeine Bhaiya'.

stories.title: 4-year-old girl shows no fear of water:Swims 900 metres across Yamuna river in 21 minutes; stuns onlookers
stories.summary: In Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh, 4-year-old Satya Bharti from the Mahewa West area has achieved a feat that even seasoned swimmers often find challenging. She swam across the Yamuna river in just 21 minutes and 28 seconds. The historic swim began at exactly 7am on Saturday. Displaying remarkable confidence and courage, Satya battled the strong currents of the Yamuna river and swam from one bank to the other, leaving everyone astonished. A video of her achievement is rapidly going viral on social media, with people widely praising her determination and bravery. Her parents and coach are extremely proud of her accomplishment. Training under coach Tribhuvan Nishad Satya is the daughter of Devendra Kumar and has been training regularly under her coach, Tribhuvan Nishad. According to him, she has shown discipline, eagerness to learn and strong confidence from a very young age. At an age when most children are just getting familiar with basic play, Satya has crossed a major river like the Yamuna, proving that with determination and proper guidance, age is no barrier to success. She has now become an inspiration not just for Prayagraj, but for the entire state. A promising future ahead Her coach believes that with advanced training, Satya has the potential to win medals for the state and the country. Meanwhile, her video continues to gain traction online, with people encouraging her and urging support to help her reach greater heights.

stories.title: Misleading video sparks FIR on 2 RJD women spokespersons:Unrest-hit Noida factories reopen after 2 days with heavy security
stories.summary: After two days of unrest, factories in Noida reopened on Wednesday, with the situation returning to normal. Heavy security has been deployed, with surveillance through CCTV cameras and drones. Around 16 companies of Rapid Action Force (RAF) and Pradeshik Armed Constabulary (PAC) have been stationed, while police conducted flag marches in Sectors 63, 80, 84, 85 and Phase 2. Notices on salary hikes have been put up outside several companies. However, some units remained shut for the day, informing employees through notices that operations would resume later, with further updates to be shared in advance. Meanwhile, an FIR has been registered at Noida’s Cyber Crime Police Station against two RJD women spokespersons, Kanchana Yadav and Priyanka Bharti. They have been accused of sharing misleading videos on social media to incite unrest and damage the image of law enforcement. District Magistrate (DM) Medha Rupam said- If any outsourcing agency or its employee causes disturbance or mischief, the agency will also be held responsible. In such a situation, the agency can be blacklisted. Its license can also be revoked. Actually, factory workers created a ruckus on Monday-Tuesday over salary increases. Stone-pelting occurred at more than 80 places. Vandalism occurred in 350 companies. Minister Anil Rajbhar said, “There is a strong whiff of a big conspiracy in this entire incident. Some anti-national forces might be involved in this.” Meanwhile, the company owners say that outsiders instigated the atmosphere. Workers can never resort to violent protests. They cannot harm the place from where they earn their livelihood. Currently, the police have arrested 396 people, including 4 women. See pictures- DM said, ‘Contractors should follow guidelines’ Union leader says, ‘No connection with agitation’ Amar Singh, District President of All India Centre Council Trade Union, says that the union has no connection with the violence and agitation. The agitation was carried out by the workers. Surendra Nahata, President of MSME Industrial Association Noida, informed that industries from Sector-1 to 6 are opening. The remaining factories will also open. Situation completely normal, no law and order problem Regarding the workers' protest in Noida, Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) Rajiv Krishna said that the situation in the district is completely normal. There is no law and order problem anywhere. All senior officers are present on the spot. The situation is being continuously monitored.

stories.title: 3 years after Atiq’s killing, wife Shaista still missing:2 other family members absconding; search continues for co-conspirators in Umesh Pal murder case
stories.summary: Three years on, the UP Police has failed to trace Atiq Ahmed’s wife Shaista Parveen. Raids were conducted across nine states, with support from ATS and RAF teams, but she remains untraceable. A reward of ₹50,000 has been announced for information on Shaista, who has been underground since the Umesh Pal murder case. She continues to feature on the UP Police’s most-wanted list of women criminals, yet her whereabouts remain unknown. Apart from Shaista, Atiq’s sister Ayesha Noori and brother Ashraf’s wife Zainab are also absconding. All three have been accused of conspiring in the Umesh Pal murder and aiding the attackers. The police have announced rewards of ₹25,000 each on Ayesha and Zainab. While there were initial suspicions that they may have fled to Dubai, officials later ruled out that possibility. Notably, Atiq Ahmed was killed on April 15, 2023. Even after three years, the police have not been able to arrest the three key accused women linked to the conspiracy. What happened over these three years, and why have they remained beyond the police’s reach? Read the full report. On February 24, 2023, lawyer Umesh Pal and his two police gunners were killed in a brutal shooting and bombing in Prayagraj’s Dhumanganj area, setting off one of Uttar Pradesh’s biggest crime probes. CCTV clues and widening conspiracy CCTV footage showed Atiq Ahmed’s son Asad firing, while Guddu Muslim hurled bombs. Others, including Ghulam, Shabir and Usman, were also seen shooting. At the time, Atiq was lodged in Sabarmati Jail, and investigators alleged he orchestrated the attack from there. He, along with brother Ashraf, son Asad and nine others, was named in the case. Within days, Atiq’s wife Shaista Parveen, sister Ayesha Noori and Ashraf’s wife Zainab were also accused of conspiracy and aiding the attackers. Notably, all three were still in the Dhumanganj area even two days after the murder. Shaista later wrote to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the Allahabad High Court Chief Justice, calling the case a political conspiracy aimed at keeping Atiq’s family out of local elections. Manhunt without breakthrough After CCTV footage was released on February 26, showing Asad firing, Shaista, Zainab and Ayesha went underground. Police launched an extensive crackdown—encounters followed, properties were demolished, and rewards were announced for information. Multiple teams carried out raids across Uttar Pradesh before expanding the search to nine states. Within weeks, more than 500 locations were searched. Several accused were caught, but the three women remained untraceable. No trace even after key killings On April 13, 2023, Asad was killed in a police encounter in Jhansi. Two days later, Atiq Ahmed and Ashraf were shot dead in Prayagraj during a medical visit. Despite these developments, none of the three women surfaced—not even for the last rites, despite heavy police surveillance. Repeated inputs placed Shaista in parts of Kaushambi, where police conducted searches using drones and combing operations, but found no trace. Assets seized, leads go cold As the search continued, authorities seized properties worth nearly ₹3,000 crore linked to Atiq’s network, many allegedly held in benami names. Investigators believe the total value could be significantly higher. CCTV clues from Meerut suggested Guddu Muslim had taken shelter at a relative’s house linked to Ayesha Noori, leading to one arrest, but Ayesha herself remained absconding. Later inputs from Odisha and Delhi also failed to yield results, though police ruled out any foreign escape. Meanwhile, the trial in the Atiq-Ashraf murder case continues, largely through video conferencing due to security concerns.

stories.title: DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts are females:Govt plans 33% women reservation in postings before 2027 polls
stories.summary: Efforts are underway in Uttar Pradesh to increase women’s participation in governance, with the first impact likely to be seen in district-level administration. The state government is preparing to assign more women IAS and IPS officers to key positions such as Divisional Commissioner, District Magistrate (DM), and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP). At present, women account for around 16% of DMs and about 12% of SSPs across the state’s 75 districts. Even before the implementation of the ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam’, the government is planning to increase women’s representation in bureaucracy to 33%. The move is aimed at sending a strong political message on women’s empowerment. Officials believe this step could help strengthen trust among women voters ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The move is being seen as part of a broader strategy: Message of empowerment: Extending ‘Nari Shakti’ beyond Parliament and Assemblies to decision-making roles like DM and SSP Targeting women voters: Of UP’s 13.39 crore voters, nearly 6.5 crore are women From beneficiaries to decision-makers: After schemes like free ration, Ujjwala and Mission Shakti, focus now shifts to representation Governance branding: Women officers are often associated with stricter law enforcement and greater sensitivity in social issues Countering opposition narrative: Aimed at addressing criticism on jobs, governance and social balance Currently, 12 out of 75 districts (16%) have women District Magistrates. This number could increase to 20–25 districts in the coming reshuffle. In policing, women IPS officers are posted in only 8 districts, indicating significant scope for expansion. Who could get key postings? Several women officers are being considered for district leadership roles, including: Annapurna Garg (IAS, 2016 batch) Kavita Meena, Vice Chairman, Muzaffarnagar Development Authority Saranjit Kaur Broca, Director, Women and Child Welfare Isha Priya, Special Secretary, Tourism Transfers likely before elections Transfers were restricted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) period from October 27, 2025 to April 10, 2026, with changes requiring Election Commission approval. With the 2027 Assembly elections expected in February–March, a major reshuffle of Commissioners, DMs and police chiefs is likely before the Model Code of Conduct comes into force, possibly by late January or early February. Election rules may trigger reshuffle As per Election Commission norms, officers posted in the same district for over three years ahead of elections are typically transferred. Apart from election-related changes, DMs of several districts—including Ambedkar Nagar, Chandauli, Hapur, Chitrakoot, Shravasti, Bhadohi, Mahoba, Sultanpur, Hathras, Barabanki and Lalitpur—may also be shifted for administrative reasons. Some may be moved to other districts, while others could be assigned roles such as Director or Special Secretary in government departments.

stories.title: Woman remains unidentified 5 days after her dead body recovery:Post-mortem report shows 17 injury marks, rape suspected
stories.summary: The post-mortem report of the unidentified woman's body found by the roadside in the Kakori area has arrived. The report shows two severe injury marks on the front and back of the woman's head, while about 15 injuries were found on other parts of the body. Doctors have stated the cause of death as severe head injury. Given the suspicion of rape, doctors have prepared slides and sent them for examination. Only after the report comes will it be known whether rape occurred or not. However, the woman has not yet been identified. Body was covered in blood On the morning of 9 April, outside Madarpur village in Kakori, the blood-soaked body of an unknown woman, approximately 35 years old, was found in a field by the roadside. Looking at the condition of the body, murder after rape was suspected. According to Inspector Satish Rathore, the woman's head had been struck with a stick or a heavy object. Injury marks were also found at several places on the body, which point towards a violent incident. So far, the woman has not been identified. For identification, photos have been pasted in public places in the city and surrounding districts. CCTV camera footage from toll plazas on Agra Expressway and other major highways is being scrutinized. No concrete clue has been found from the crime scene or the woman's clothes that could help identify her. The investigation into the case is ongoing. Unidentified body was cremated Due to lack of identification, the police cremated the woman's body on April 13. DNA samples have been preserved for future identification. A case of murder has been registered against unknown persons in the matter. ACP Kakori Shakeel Ahmed said that so far, footage from more than 500 CCTV cameras has been scanned for the identification of the woman. Pictures of the body have been circulated on social media platforms. Missing person cases registered in nearby districts are also being investigated.

stories.title: Parents plan to sell their newborn fails:Grandmother rescues child; mother had struck a deal with businessman for 2.5 lakhs
stories.summary: In Agra, a mother made a deal to sell her two-day-old newborn baby. The price of the baby was fixed at Rs 2.5 lakh. A businessman even reached the hospital to take the baby, but the grandmother and aunt got wind of it. Both of them filed a complaint on the Child Helpline. As soon as the information was received, the team reached the spot. Immediate action was taken with the help of police. The newborn and family members were taken into custody. Everyone was presented before the magistrate of the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). On Monday, the magistrate had the couple fill an affidavit. After this, the newborn was handed over to them. Now know the complete case A call came to Childline's helpline number 1098 on Friday night. The woman who called, identified herself as Rajkumari. Rajkumari said that her son Manoj lives in Shastripuram, Sikandra. Manoj works as a laborer in a factory. His wife Kumkum has a son from before. “Kumkum gave birth to a second son at the hospital on Wednesday. The child is being sold right after birth. A deal has already been made with a trader from Kamla Nagar. A deal has been fixed for two and a half lakh rupees to hand over the newborn. The trader was supposed to reach the hospital on Friday night to take the child,” she said. Childline team reached the hospital, couple denied the allegations As soon as the complaint was received, the Childline team reached the hospital with the police. The team spoke with the woman who gave birth to the newborn and her husband. The couple flatly denied the allegations of selling the child. They claimed that some relatives were making false allegations as part of a conspiracy. After this, with the help of police, the child and family members were presented before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). Here, an affidavit was filled by the couple. After completing the procedure, the newborn was handed back to the couple. Grandmother said - They were selling the newborn for two and a half lakh Grandmother Rajkumari said - On Friday, my daughter-in-law gave birth to a son at Lady Lion Hospital. Just a short while later, some people arrived at the hospital to see the child. Those people were talking about buying the child. I wanted to bring my grandson home. The son, daughter-in-law, and father-in-law were going to give away the child for two and a half lakh rupees. I opposed this, but no one listened to me. Angered by this, I returned home. After some time, my daughter called, so I told her the whole matter. Child reunited with family after two days of surveillance Rajkumari said that my daughter immediately complained to Agra Child Helpline number 1098 from Meerut. After this, the team reached the spot and action was initiated. Due to Saturday and Sunday being holidays, further proceedings could not take place. The Childline team deployed police personnel outside the hospital. The police kept surveillance for two days so that no one could take the child away. On Monday, we were presented before the magistrate of the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). After filling out an affidavit there, further action was taken. Now the child is at our home and we are happy. Child will have to be presented again after 15 days Childline coordinator Brajesh Kumar Gautam said- On Monday, the couple was presented before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). Here, a written affidavit was taken from the couple. It was clarified in the affidavit that they will not give the newborn to any other person for adoption. After completing the procedure, the child has been handed over to the couple. They have been instructed that the child will have to be presented before the committee again within 15 days.

stories.title: Clouds hover over Hyderabad on April 21 afternoon
Dhirendra Shastri says, 'Temples crowded, now need ‘storm’ on streets':Plans Rudrabhishek at Gyanvapi; addresses Hanumant Katha in Prayagraj
stories.summary: The Peethadhishwar of Bageshwar Dham, Pandit Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, has a Hanumant Katha (religious discourse) in Prayagraj starting today. He arrived at Bamrauli Airport by helicopter. From here, he traveled by car to Karela Bagh, then reached Arail Selfie Point by steamer on the Yamuna. Upon Dhirendra Shastri's arrival, devotees chanted slogans hailing Bageshwar Baba. A grand pandal (tent) has been constructed over 13,000 square meters at the Katha venue on the Yamuna bank. The three-day Katha is expected to attract over 5 lakh devotees. The pandal has seating arrangements for approximately 20-22 thousand devotees. The entire event is being organized over an area of about six acres. Eight entry gates have been constructed in the pandal for devotees to enter and exit. Surveillance is being conducted with 3000 police personnel along with 500 CCTVs and drones. Among the huge crowd gathered to listen to Dhirendra Shastri's Katha, one devotee has arrived in a wheelchair. See 2 pictures The patron of the Hanumant Katha is BJP leader Dr. Uday Pratap Singh, a resident of Prayagraj. He is the Director of Harinarayan Group of Colleges. He has a total of five colleges. Apart from this, he has a rice mill. His father had a factory in Mirpur. Later, Uday Pratap started doing property business. Dr. Uday Pratap Singh has also met Home Minister Amit Shah several times. He is also close to Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya. He has organized many programs before this as well. These have included Bollywood actress and MP Kangana Ranaut, cricketer Suresh Raina, Bhojpuri actress Akshara Singh, singer Hansraj Raghuwanshi, and many other film artists.

stories.title: Groom’s uncle left behind by baraat in Jhansi:Later found hanging from tree 100 metres from guest house; suicide suspected
stories.summary: In Jhansi, the wedding procession bus moved ahead without the groom's uncle being seated. This made him angry. His daughter and son-in-law persuaded him and stopped the bus to make him board. After this, the wedding procession reached the wedding venue. There, the uncle gave his purse and mobile to his daughter, then went missing. In the morning, his body was found hanging from a tree about 100 meters away from the wedding venue. Family members said that the driver of the bus carrying the wedding procession had stopped the vehicle on the way for some work. The groom's uncle, who was traveling in it, got down to urinate. Meanwhile, the bus started moving. People stopped the bus about 20 meters ahead. However, the uncle refused to board the bus. The matter is from Month town. Know the complete matter in detail Ishwar Singh (57), a resident of Joohi area in Kanpur, was an electrician by profession. His cousin brother Agan Kumar lives in Rajpur in Kanpur Dehat. Agan's son Manoj's wedding was fixed in Jhansi. To attend that wedding, he first went to Rajpur. Then from there, he went to Jhansi on the wedding bus. Ishwar Singh's son Rohit Verma said that the wedding procession left from Kanpur Dehat on Monday evening for Month in Jhansi. When the bus stopped on the way, Papa also got down to urinate. Meanwhile, the bus started moving. When he raised an alarm, the bus was stopped about 15 to 20 meters ahead. He got angry about this. Then his sister and brother-in-law pacified him and made him sit in the bus. At night, the wedding procession reached Pitambara in Month. Disappeared with daughter's purse and mobile Son Rohit said - Father did not go inside the wedding venue. He gave his mobile and purse to sister outside and left. Sister tried to stop him, but he didn't listen. Sister called out, but the DJ was playing so no one could hear. Sister went inside and brought family members, but by then father had already left. After this, a search was started for him, but no clue was found. On Tuesday morning, he was being searched for again. Meanwhile, about 100 meters away from the wedding venue, the father was found hanging from a tree in the bushes with a noose made from a gamcha (towel). After this, people from the surrounding area gathered and informed the police. The police have sent the body for post-mortem. Nephew Yogendra said that uncle Ishwar Singh was mentally disturbed. His treatment was also ongoing. He would get very angry over small matters. This is why he committed suicide. After the suicide, mourning spread at the wedding venue. Family members reached the spot crying and wailing. Ishwar has 2 sons Rohit and Mohit. Neither of them is married, while daughter Neha is already married.
