stories.title: Vrindavan boat tragedy:Manager’s body surfaces on 7th day after swelling; divers search 30 km area
stories.summary: The body of missing Pankaj Malhotra has been recovered on the seventh day after the boat accident in the Yamuna river in Vrindavan. His body was found about 2.5 kilometres downstream from the accident site, near Devrha Ghat and beneath the Panigaon bridge. The body had surfaced due to swelling, and divers along with army personnel, pulled it out. With this, the death toll in the incident has risen to 16. Earlier, on Monday at around 8 am, the body of a woman was found at Bengali Ghat, about 12 kilometres from the accident site, while a youth's body was recovered near the Deora Baba Ashram. The woman was identified as Monika Tandon from Ludhiana. She had come with her mother-in-law, Savita. She had been married just six months ago, and her husband lives abroad. Monika was also planning to go abroad soon. On the day of the accident, she was sitting in the boat with her neighbour Dinky, whose body had been found on April 12. The youth was identified as 22-year-old Yash Bhalla, also from Ludhiana. He had come to Vrindavan for the first time and was associated with the Banke Bihari group. He used to play the dholak during religious singing events. In a video recorded before the boat capsized, Yash can be seen playing the dholak. His elder brother is an accountant, his mother Sunita is a homemaker, and his father sells clothes on a street cart. According to officials, the bodies had floated to the surface of the river. After the post-mortem, both bodies were handed over to their families. The accident took place on Friday, October 10, at around 3 pm when the boat capsized. Since then, the search for Pankaj Malhotra had become a major challenge for the police and administration. Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), and local divers had been continuously carrying out a search operation in the Yamuna River. Around 250 personnel were involved in the operation. Read the full case in detail below Pankaj had come to Vrindavan on April 10 Rural SP Suresh Chandra Rawat said that Pankaj Malhotra was a manager in a steel company in Himachal. He had come alone to Vrindavan on April 10. He was boating in the Yamuna with a group when the boat overturned and he drowned. A rescue operation had been ongoing to find him. On the seventh day after the accident, his body was found near Devrha Baba Ghat. His family has been informed, and the body will be handed over after the post-mortem. Brother said Pankaj used to visit Mathura every year Aniket said Pankaj Malhotra was his cousin. “We are deeply saddened by his death. We had been waiting here for several days, hoping his body would be found. Today, we finally got him. He used to come to Mathura every year with his family. He was married and had two children, a three-year-old daughter and a nine-year-old son. He had two sisters and was the eldest among them. Five to six members of his extended family have also died in this accident.” How did the accident happen? A youth who survived said the boat was about 50 feet from the bank in the middle of the Yamuna River. The wind was blowing at around 40 km per hour. The boat suddenly started shaking, and the boatman lost control. Tourists asked him to stop as they were nearing a bridge, but he did not listen. The boat narrowly avoided hitting the bridge twice, but on the third attempt, it collided and capsized. Timeline: From accident to rescue operation On April 10 at around 3 pm, a boat carrying 38 devotees capsized near Kesi Ghat, about 2 kilometres from the Banke Bihari temple. On the same day, 22 people were rescued, while 10 bodies were recovered. Teams from the army, NDRF, SDRF, PAC and local divers began search operations. At around 12:30 am, the submerged steamer was pulled out using a crane. Rescue teams had hoped to find bodies inside the steamer, but none were found. The search team was then expanded to 250 members. On April 11, one body — Manik Tandon — was recovered, taking the toll to 11. On the same day, contractor Narayan and boatman Pankaj were arrested. On April 12, two more bodies — Rishabh and Dinky — were found. On April 13, a woman’s body was found at Bengali Ghat and a man’s body near Deora Baba Ashram. On April 14, the bodies of Yash Bhalla and Monika Tandon were recovered, taking the toll to 15. On April 16, the body of Pankaj Malhotra was recovered. Four people were made to get off before the accident Rajinder Kaur said there were 37 people on the steamer. The boat stopped midway, and when passengers asked why, the boatman told them to shift to another boat. Women refused, but four elderly people moved to the other boat. She said the boat was not overloaded, as she had travelled in it before. Bridge came towards us, rope got stuck Rajinder Kaur said while the steamer was stationary, the bridge appeared to be moving towards them. The operator said he would cross before the bridge arrived, but it approached quickly and hit the boat. The boat got stuck in a rope attached to the bridge and overturned. The bridge structure then fell over the boat. I was standing and recording video She said she was standing and recording when the boat overturned, and she held onto it. When the bridge fell over, she let go and went underwater. People trapped beneath the boat could not escape. Boat hit my head five times She said

stories.title: 38-year-old man dies after ambulance runs out of oxygen:Fuel also exhausted during transfer from Rampur to Moradabad
stories.summary: A 38-year-old man died after an ambulance carrying him ran out of both oxygen and fuel while he was being shifted from Rampur to Moradabad. The victim had sustained critical injuries after being hit by a tractor. After receiving primary treatment at a district hospital, doctors referred him to Meerut. However, his family decided to take him to Moradabad in a privately hired ambulance. According to family members, the patient was on oxygen support, but the oxygen supply ran out mid-way. Soon after, the ambulance also ran out of fuel, forcing it to stop on the road. The man died shortly thereafter. Accident and Medical referral The incident occurred late Wednesday night in Ahmadnagar Jibai village under Shahzadnagar police station limits in Rampur. The deceased, Kuldeep Singh (38), a farmer, was heading to his field on a motorcycle around 10 pm amid the wheat harvesting season when a speeding tractor hit him, leaving him critically injured. Family members rushed him to the district hospital, where doctors provided emergency treatment and referred him to Meerut due to his serious condition. Oxygen depletion and Ambulance breakdown Kuldeep’s nephew, Harvinder Singh, said the family had barely covered half the distance to Moradabad when the oxygen cylinder in the ambulance got depleted. “We asked the driver to speed up, but shortly after that, the ambulance ran out of fuel as well. Due to lack of oxygen, Kuldeep died,” he said. Family vandalises ambulance, driver flees Angered by the death, the family vandalised the ambulance, while the driver fled the scene. Police were informed and later sent the body for postmortem. The ambulance has been seized at Majhola police station in Moradabad, and further action is underway. Mandatory standards for ambulances As per regulations, ambulances must comply with strict operational standards. These include valid registration and permits, trained drivers and paramedical staff, and a functional oxygen supply at all times. They must also be equipped with a stretcher, first-aid kit, and basic life support (BLS) systems, and remain operational 24×7 with proper fuel and technical readiness. Possible legal action in such cases For critical patients, advanced life support (ALS) facilities are also required. Any negligence in maintaining these standards can invite strict action. Legal provisions may include charges under IPC Section 304A (causing death by negligence), and Sections 279/336/337/338 (endangering life). Authorities may also suspend or cancel the ambulance’s permit, arrest those responsible, and provide compensation to the victim’s family.

stories.title: Yogi vows strict action against mafias in Bengal:Says, 'They will be made to fall in line'; urges people not to fear
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath addressed a rally in Asansol, West Bengal, saying people should not fear “TMC goons, mafias, or clerics.” Yogi, who is one of the star campaigners, while campaigning for the saffron party on Thursday, asserted that if the BJP comes to power in the state, such elements would “fall in line” and even be seen “sweeping the streets.” “Do not be afraid of what TMC’s goons say. Do not be intimidated by Mafias or concerned about what clerics say. Let the BJP form the government, and all of them will start flattering you”, he said. Claims of better law and order in Uttar Pradesh Adityanath highlighted the law-and-order situation in Uttar Pradesh, claiming that no one is allowed to offer Namaz on roads and that festivals are celebrated peacefully. “There is no hooliganism. Women are safe. Only the BJP and a double-engine government can guarantee this,” he said. Remarks on Religion and Politics CM also accused West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee of being “averse to Ram Naam and Durga Puja,” adding that similar attitudes existed earlier in Uttar Pradesh before the BJP came to power. He said the construction of the Ram temple in Ayodhya was made possible after the BJP double-engine government came to power, asserting that neither Congress, the Samajwadi Party, nor the TMC could stop it. “Only Prime Minister Narendra Modi can guarantee no riots, no curfew. We will not allow cow slaughter or division among Hindus,” he added. Multiple rallies across Bengal Adityanath held three public meetings in West Bengal on Thursday as part of the Assembly election campaign. He first addressed a rally in Asansol, followed by events in Birbhum and Bolpur, seeking support for BJP and NDA candidates. Key points from the speech 1. BJP government as solution to ‘Mafia rule’ Adityanath alleged that central funds sent by Prime Minister Narendra Modi for public welfare are “siphoned off by TMC goons.” He said Uttar Pradesh faced similar issues nine years ago, with frequent riots, unsafe conditions for women, and widespread crime. “The only solution to anarchy, fear, riots, and mafia rule is a BJP double-engine government,” he said. 2. ‘No curfew, no riots in UP now’ He claimed that strict action against mafias inUP, including property seizures and use of bulldozers, has ended organized crime. “Today, there is no curfew, no riots in UP—everything is fine. Earlier, people had to agitate for Ram Janmabhoomi, and devotees were fired upon,” he said. 3. Opposition accused of ruining Bengal Adityanath said West Bengal was once India’s cultural capital but alleged that Congress, Left parties, and TMC have turned it into a “crime capital.” “There was development, farmers were happy, and youth had jobs. Now it has become a center of anarchy, corruption, and fear. Mafias dominate resources, and jobs have disappeared,” he claimed. Inauguration of security buildings in Gorakhpur Earlier in the day, Adityanath inaugurated new security buildings in Gorakhpur, constructed at a cost of ₹9.18 crore to enhance security in the Gorakhnath temple area. The facilities will house offices of senior police officials, a control room, storage, and maintenance units. Strengthening policing infrastructure 1. Accommodation for 100 personnel Adityanath said the building can accommodate up to 100 police personnel and officers, with all necessary facilities. He added that in 55 districts, the tallest buildings will now belong to the police. 2. Security as foundation of good governance “Security is the first condition of good governance,” he said, emphasizing the need for proper training and infrastructure for police personnel. He noted that when his government came to power in 2017, more than half the police posts were vacant. “In nine years, we have recruited over 2.19 lakh personnel,” he added.

stories.title: Mercury crosses 44°C in UP for first time this season:Lions and deer cooled with sprays; rhino gets mud pool
stories.summary: Severe heat has started in UP. On Wednesday, for the first time this season, the maximum temperature crossed 44 °C. Not only this, mercury was recorded at 40 degrees or more in 16 districts. The effect of increasing heat is now visible on zoo animals as well. To provide relief from the heat, a mud pond has been built for rhinoceroses in Kanpur. Water sprays are being used on deer and lions. Expert Dr. Nasir said that rhinoceroses keep themselves cool by rolling in the mud. Wet soil sticks to their bodies, which provides relief to the rhinos from the heat. Talking about the last 24 hours, Banda was the hottest, where the day temperature was recorded at 44.8C. Apart from this, mercury was recorded at 43C in Prayagraj, 42.8C in Varanasi, 41.4C in Jhansi, and 41.3C in Sultanpur. Hot winds are making it feel like a heatwave during the day. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- There are no chances of rain for the next 10 days. Westerly winds are now weakening. Due to this, the mercury will jump by 3 to 6C in the next 4-5 days. In the coming days, temperatures in most districts will reach up to 45 degrees. The impact of heat will intensify. There is also a possibility of heatwave. stories.title: Massive fire in 200 huts in Ghaziabad, cylinders explode:Smoke visible from 10 km away; 22 fire tenders deployed
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in around 500 slum huts in Kanawani village under the Indirapuram police station area of Ghaziabad at around 12:00 noon on Thursday. The fire was so intense that massive flames were visible from nearly 10 km away, triggering panic in the area as residents rushed out of their homes. Local residents immediately informed the fire department. Soon after receiving the alert, about eight fire trucks reached the spot. Considering the seriousness of the situation, additional fire brigade vehicles were also called from Noida. Firefighters are continuously trying to bring the blaze under control. It is being reported that the huts contained large quantities of plastic, wood, and other highly flammable materials, which caused the fire to spread rapidly and made firefighting operations difficult. People in nearby residential areas faced breathing difficulties because of heavy smoke, and many residents stepped out of their homes as a precaution. According to eyewitnesses, fire engulfed several huts within a short time. However, no casualties have been reported so far. The cause of the fire is still unknown. Fire department teams and the local administration are present at the spot and are closely monitoring the situation. Pictures of the incident Eyewitnesses said around 150–200 huts were gutted in the Ghaziabad fire, with losses running into lakhs as the blaze reportedly started during cooking and spread rapidly due to cylinder blasts. About 22 fire tenders were deployed, bringing nearly 90 per cent of the fire under control while preventing it from spreading to nearby residential areas. Residents said entire households were reduced to ashes, affecting around 200–250 people. Authorities have deployed ambulances, alerted hospitals and said a survey will be conducted if anyone is reported missing, while the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

stories.title: Bulldozer action on Eidgah and Imambara in Sambhal:Crowd dispersed; heavy police and PAC deployed
stories.summary: Bulldozer action began at 8:00 am on Thursday on an Eidgah and an Imambara in Sambhal. The Imambara has already been demolished, and the Eidgah is now being razed using four bulldozers. Police personnel from five police stations and one company of Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) have been deployed at the site. Meanwhile, villagers gathered at the spot, but officials removed them due to fear of possible protest. According to the administration, the Eidgah was built on about 7 bighas of grazing land, while the Imambara had been constructed on land meant for a manure pit. Following complaints from villagers, Lekhpal Sparsh Gupta filed an appeal in the Tehsildar court on 18 January. On 31 January, a notice was published in newspapers as per court orders, asking any occupants to come forward. However, no one responded. On Thursday morning around 7:30 am, SDM Nidhi Patel and Naib Tehsildar Deepak Kumar Jurail reached the site with a team. Some people were seen trying to demolish the Imambara using chisels and hammers, but the administration removed them. The incident took place in Bicholi village under the Kotwali Sambhal police station area. DM and SP reach the spot Around 12 noon, Rajendra Pensiya and Krishna Kumar Vishnoi also reached the site. They reviewed the report on the demolition of the structures from police and administrative teams and issued necessary instructions. Imambara wall collapses on JCB in Sambhal, operator injured JCB operator Saurabh Sirswal of the Nagar Palika Parishad Sambhal suffered an injury to his right hand when an Imambara wall suddenly collapsed onto the machine during demolition. The glass of the JCB broke, and the machine was also damaged in the incident. Following the accident, the machine developed a fault and was sent back from the site. Temples built on govt land should also be demolished Villager Zubaida said, Demolition action should be stopped. She stated that the Imambara and Eidgah were used by everyone in the area, and even wedding processions of poor families used to stay there. She questioned that if the issue is construction on government land, then temples built on government land should also face action, but currently, action is being taken only against mosques. She added that if the law is equal for everyone, then action should also be taken against temples built on government land. Structures built on encroached grazing and pit land Nidhi Patel, SDM of Sambhal, said, The constructions had been carried out by encroaching on grazing land and pit land, and the demolition action is being carried out on the orders of the Tehsildar court. stories.title: Yogi warns of strict action against police attacks:Says over 2 lakh vacancies filled in 8 years; inaugurates security buildings
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is in Gorakhpur today. He said that the first condition of good governance is security. Efforts are made at the government level for this. There used to be a belief that for security, just recruit police. But if police personnel are not trained, then they are also ordinary people. Therefore, after the recruitment process, their training should happen. After that, when they perform their duty, the infrastructure facilities during that time should also be of that standard, this was not paid attention to. The result of this was that the police personnel were not able to fulfill their responsibilities. Yogi said- We have increased police facilities When we came in 2017, at that time more than half the posts in Uttar Pradesh Police were vacant. In 9 years, we have done recruitment of more than 2 lakh 19 thousand. When we came to government in 2017, the training capacity of police was not more than 3 thousand at a time. Currently, as a result of the development of infrastructure facilities, we are training more than 60 thousand police personnel. The state is the same, but now facilities have increased more than 200 times. Earlier, whether it was police station, outpost, police lines or PAC battalion, there were no residential facilities for police personnel anywhere. The result was that they lived on rent or somehow spent their life. Residential facilities for 200 police personnel were provided in every police line. What the model of a police station will be, you can see Gorakhnath police station. Buildings for fire tenders are being built rapidly. When infrastructure facilities developed, their work speed also increased. The result was that a better security model was created. Earlier, the CM inaugurated the security buildings. These have been constructed for the security of the Gorakhnath Temple area. The construction of both buildings cost Rs 9 crore 18 lakh. Both buildings are adjacent to each other. Both buildings have been constructed as stilt plus 4 floors. The Additional Superintendent of Police, Deputy Superintendent of Police office and control room will be located here. Along with this, a police store room and maintenance workshop have also been built in it.

stories.title: 2 children burnt alive, 250 families homeless in Lucknow fire:Women allege huts were deliberately set ablaze
stories.summary: Two children were burnt alive in a massive fire that broke out on Wednesday in a cluster of huts in Lucknow. Nearly 250 families living in the slum area were left homeless after the blaze destroyed their homes. DCP Diksha Sharma said efforts are underway to identify the victims’ families. On Thursday morning, only ashes and burnt household belongings could be seen at the site. Several families were searching through the debris for whatever they could recover, while police asked people to move away from the area. The District Magistrate arranged shelter for many affected families in night shelters, while some spent the night on a nearby vacant plot. Women from the settlement alleged that residents of nearby houses had earlier threatened them to vacate the huts, warning of consequences if they refused. They claimed the huts were deliberately set on fire after they did not leave. They also said their lifelong savings were reduced to ashes, adding that some belongings could have been saved if the fire brigade had arrived earlier. Police deployment has been increased in the Vikasnagar area amid fears of tension. Security personnel with helmets and batons are stationed at the site. Key details of the incident The fire broke out around 5:30 pm on Wednesday in Vikasnagar, one of the posh areas of the city. During the blaze, more than 30 LPG cylinders exploded, and over 250 huts were destroyed. Smoke from the fire was visible from nearly 10 km away. As a precaution, residents of 20 nearby houses were evacuated. Around 20 fire brigade vehicles worked for nearly five hours to control the fire. Electricity supply in the area was temporarily cut during the operation. Rajnath Singh, the Member of Parliament from Lucknow, spoke to District Magistrate Vishakh G to review the situation, while Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak also visited the spot to assess the situation. stories.title: Over 250 huts gutted in fire as 30 cylinders explode:Flames visible up to 10 kilometres; man says, '4 children burnt alive'
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in Lucknow on Wednesday evening at 5:30 PM. This fire in the Vikasnagar area caused more than 30 cylinders to explode. Over 250 huts and small housing units were reduced to ashes. Flames were visible from about 10 kilometers away. After the fire broke out, around 20 nearby houses were evacuated. 20 fire brigade vehicles brought the fire under control after about 3 hours. During this time, electricity in the area was cut off. When it became dark, rescue operations were carried out using generator-powered lights. A young man claims that his 4 children died in the fire. All belongings of other people were reduced to ashes. Those whose huts burned kept crying and wailing. Some people allege that the fire was set deliberately. CM Yogi took cognizance of the fire incident and immediately directed officials to reach the spot. Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak also reached the spot and ordered officials to expedite rescue operations. First see the pictures of the massive fire People said - Everything I had turned to ashes Local resident Aman Gupta said that the fire broke out at 5:30. After the fire, there was mourning and chaos in the settlement. A woman, Shamsunisha, said while crying - The entire family was at home when the fire broke out. Now there is no trace of the family. Our house has completely burned to ashes. Pooja said - Wedding preparations were going on at home. My brother-in-law's son's wedding procession was about to leave. All the wedding items burned in the fire. People somehow saved their lives. Meanwhile, a woman fainted while searching for family members. People present at the spot took her to the hospital. A victim Rahman said while crying - My 4 children have been burnt. I have my mother, no father. My children were playing at home. I saw that a fire had broken out. As soon as I reached there, I saw my children had been burnt. My 4 children died in the fire. Prema said that she has small children. All the children's clothes were burnt in the fire. It is not known how the fire started. All the household items turned to ash. The grain was also completely burnt. Now there is nothing left to eat. Several cows were also burned in the fire incident. Animal Welfare Officer Abhinav Verma also reached the spot. He informed that the injured stray animals from the accident have been sent to the Municipal Corporation's cow shelter. Two cows are being treated and 6 have been rescued. People's anger visible after the fire After the fire, anger was visible among the people. Angry people created a ruckus outside the plot owner's house. Women alleged that they were threatened to vacate the slum. People accused the plot owner of setting the fire. Police dragged out the youth to control the situation. Even after this, people continued to create a ruckus for a long time. However, the land where the fire broke out is said to belong to LDA. According to local people, there is a dispute over the land. The matter of compensation between farmers and the authority is pending. A large number of huts were built here. Most people worked as laborers. Many people also worked as rag pickers. The number of people residing here from Assam is said to be higher. DG Fire said- Large number of gas cylinders found DG Fire Sujit Pandey said- As soon as information about the fire was received, fire engines were immediately sent to the spot from nearby fire stations including BKT and Indira Nagar. More than 20 fire engines worked together to extinguish the fire and prevented it from spreading to nearby areas in time. The relief is that there is no information about any loss of life so far. He said that a large number of gas cylinders have been recovered in this incident, which could be a major reason for the rapid spread of the fire. Currently, the entire matter is being investigated and the situation is being continuously monitored. After the fire, the NDRF team reached the spot to control the deteriorating situation. Traffic jam from Munshi Puliya to Engineering College As soon as information about the fire in Vikas Nagar was received, ambulances and fire brigades started reaching the spot. This caused severe traffic jam in the area. The road from Munshi Puliya to Engineering College intersection remained jammed for about 3 hours. Vehicles remained stuck on the flyover for hours as well. Rajnath told DM - Speed up relief and rescue work Defense Minister Rajnath Singh took cognizance of the matter and spoke to the District Magistrate over the phone. He gave instructions to speed up relief work. He asked to ensure all possible assistance for the affected people and to arrange proper treatment for the injured. According to BJP Lucknow Metropolitan President Anand Dwivedi, the Defense Minister has expressed deep concern over the incident and has given instructions to the administration to provide immediate help. Meanwhile, DM Vishakh G said that people affected by the fire have been shifted to rain basera (night shelter). Brajesh Pathak said - Government is with the affected families Taking cognizance of the fire in the Vikas Nagar area, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak immediately reached the spot. He said that a high-level investigation will be conducted into this incident. The government stands with the affected families. The Deputy CM called health department teams on the spot and gave instructions to provide better treatment to the people injured in the incident. He instructed officials to speed up relief work. The Deputy CM discussed rescue operations in this incident with the District Magistrate, Police Commissioner, Chief Development Officer, Municipal Commissioner, NDRF and other officials at the incident site itself. Akhilesh said - Victims should get immediate treatment and help Former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav has also reacted to this incident and demanded swift action from the government. He said - Immediate arrangements for food and water should be made for the victims. The injured should get immediate treatment and alternative accommodation arrangements should be ensured for the affected families. Akhilesh demanded a thorough investigation of this fire incident and said that keeping in mind the side of the poor, every aspect should be investigated and the situation regarding those who are missing should also be clarified.

stories.title: Ghaziabad police gun down 4-year-old niece’s rape-murder accused:2 constables injured during operation
stories.summary: In Ghaziabad, police shot dead a man accused of raping his 4-year-old niece in an encounter: two constables were also injured during the exchange of fire on Sunday and admitted to hospital. The accused, Jasim alias Chhotu, carried a ₹50,000 police reward. Know the complete case... Jasim alias Chhotu (25) was a resident of Sisauli area in Muzaffarnagar. He was living in a rented accommodation in the Tila police station area of Ghaziabad and worked as a labourer. His sister lived with her family around 100 metres away from his room. On April 11 (Saturday), he had gone to his sister’s house. The child’s father stated that around 1 PM, his brother-in-law Chhotu arrived at the house and took his daughter with him on the pretext of going for a walk. When the girl did not return home till late evening, he went to Chhotu’s room. The girl was not there. When asked about her, the accused allegedly said that he had left the child outside their house. After this, the father and mother became worried and started searching for the girl, but she could not be found. When she was still missing till late evening, a complaint was filed at the police station. Police circulated the girl’s photograph to nearby police stations. Late at night, information was received about a girl’s body found on Bikaner 80 Foota Road. On receiving the information, the family reached the spot and identified the body as their daughter. In the complaint given to police, the father alleged that his brother-in-law took the child to his house on the pretext of feeding her. He raped her there, then strangled her to death. After that, he shifted the body about 500 metres away to Bikaner 80 Foota Road, where it was dumped under a car before he returned to his room. The news is being updated

stories.title: Thar runs over brother and sister drinking juice in Mathura:Vehicle overturns after hitting shop, driver, a farmer leader, flees
stories.summary: In Mathura, a speeding Thar ran over a brother and sister standing by the roadside. Both were sitting on a red scooter outside a juice shop, drinking juice. Suddenly, a Thar vehicle hit the scooter from behind. Then, it overturned after crushing the brother and sister. Both were seriously injured in this accident. A farmer leader's sticker is affixed to the rear window of the Thar. It is thus believed that the farmer leader himself was driving the vehicle, who fled the scene immediately after the accident. CCTV footage of this incident started being rapidly shared on social media on Sunday. The time of the incident appears to be Saturday evening at 4:26 PM. The case is from the Thana Highway area. 3 pictures of the incident Then a red Thar car comes from behind, and it runs over the brother and sister along with the scooter. Know what is visible in the video It is clearly visible in the video that a red scooter is parked on the footpath by the roadside. A girl is sitting on it. A boy is standing in front of her. Both are eating and drinking something and talking to each other. Just then, a red Thar comes from behind at high speed. The Thar swerved. Then, hitting the scooter parked by the roadside, it also ran over the girl and the boy. After this, it collided with the shop and overturned. Seeing this, a crowd of nearby people gathered. Accident near Mata Temple Khushboo (23) and her brother Rajkumar (20) live in Bhagatipuram Colony, Aurangabad. On Saturday evening, around 4:30 PM, Khushboo was sitting on a scooter outside the Mata Temple near Chandanvan Colony, while her brother Rajkumar was standing there. Both were talking. During this, a red colored, high-speed Thar vehicle, out of control, collided with the scooter, crushing Khushboo and Rajkumar. In the accident, Khushboo sustained deep injuries to both her legs and head. Her right leg had to be amputated. Meanwhile, Rajkumar sustained serious injuries to his shoulder. The family members are getting the brother and sister treated in the hospital. It was reported that both siblings had come to Chandanvan Colony to drink juice. In this matter, Thana Highway in-charge Shailendra Singh stated that no complaint has been received yet. The ownership of the vehicle is being investigated. The family members are saying that they will first get their children treated, and only after that will they discuss anything further. Thar vehicle belongs to farmer leader The Thar vehicle (UP 85 BW 5248) that ran over the brother and sister does not even have a number plate at the back. On the rear window of the vehicle, it is written 'State President Western Uttar Pradesh Bhartiya Kisan Union (A)'. After the accident, the youth driving the Thar fled the scene. It is suspected that the Thar belongs to a farmer leader. The out-of-control Thar vehicle that overturned was straightened with the help of a crane. Only then did people passing on the road get relief from the traffic jam. -

stories.title: Gangrape survivor creates 40-minute chaos in Rampur mosque:Breaks glass, burns items, locks gate despite police presence
stories.summary: A gangrape survivor in Rampur created a major disturbance on Saturday by entering a mosque and vandalising it. She broke window panes and is also accused of burning religious books, a sheet and other items. She even locked the mosque from outside. At the time of the incident, a woman sub-inspector and three constables were also present with her, as she was under police protection following a High Court order. The woman continued the disturbance for nearly 40 minutes. A video of the incident has also surfaced. She is a fashion designer and make-up artist by profession. She has filed a gangrape and property grab case against four of her maternal uncles and 13 others. Two of the accused uncles are village heads of different villages, while one has been a district panchayat member for the past 25 years. Police have arrested the woman and one of her associates and sent them to jail. One accused is still absconding. The incident took place in the Shahzadnagar police station area. Now read the entire matter in a sequential manner... The victim is originally from Moradabad and has her maternal family in Dabka village under Shahzadnagar area of Rampur. Her case is being heard in the Rampur Sessions Court, and she had a scheduled hearing on Saturday. After the hearing, around 3 pm, she directly went to a mosque in the village. Before the security personnel accompanying her could react, she entered the mosque, broke window glasses, brought out items from inside and set them on fire. After this, she locked the main gate of the mosque from outside. Members of the mosque committee and local residents tried to stop her, but she became even more aggressive. She also misbehaved with people passing by. She grabbed the collar of an elderly man riding a bicycle and assaulted him. A video of the incident went viral on social media. Late on Saturday night around 10:30 pm, police registered a case at Shahzadnagar police station against the woman, her associate Azeem, and an unidentified person. Case of gangrape, kidnapping, property grabbing against maternal uncles Police said the woman’s maternal village is Dabka. She works in Mumbai as a fashion designer and make-up artist for models. Her father died in 2012. On 21 March 2024, she filed a case in Delhi against four maternal uncles and 14 others, accusing them of gangrape, kidnapping and grabbing property. The accused reportedly have close political connections. The case was transferred from Delhi Police to Rampur Police on 21 March 2024. Four accused were arrested but later granted bail by the High Court. Accused have political influence, got case transferred to Sambhal-Bijnor According to her lawyer Arif Khan, the accused used political influence to first get the case transferred from Rampur to Sambhal. In Sambhal, a trainee woman IPS officer investigated the case. Later, the case was transferred to Bijnor. In Bijnor Kotwali, then Inspector Crime Phoolchand Burma filed a final report in court, stating the allegations were false due to lack of evidence. The court dismissed the case and acquitted all four accused. Appeal in High Court, Instructions to Lower Court Challenging the lower court decision, the woman filed a petition in the High Court. The High Court directed that the case be transferred back to the lower court and ordered the Rampur SP to conduct a fresh investigation. The court also directed that she be provided police protection on every date of hearing. On Saturday, after the hearing, she left the court and went to Dabka village, where she created the disturbance at the mosque located in front of accused uncle Bablu’s house. During the incident, a woman sub-inspector and three constables deployed for her security were also present. Now read the young woman's complete allegation The woman said her mother is the only child of her maternal grandparents and there is 350 bigha of land in her grandfather’s name. After her father’s death, her maternal uncle Imtiaz Hussain alias Chintu brought her mother to his house and allegedly kept her confined for 14 years to take control of the property. She further alleged that about nine months ago she reached Dabka village and, with police help, rescued her mother and sent her to a relative in Moradabad, where her twin sister also lives. After that she went to Delhi. On 29 February, she again came to Dabka village to collect land documents. She had obtained papers from the court, after which a dispute occurred. She said that the video of her was made by the mosque’s maulana in front of uncle Bablu’s house. She claimed the accused were angered after she obtained the documents. On 13 March at around 7 pm, uncle Imtiaz Hussain alias Chintu, Irfan Hussain alias Pappu (village head of nearby Chamaraua village), Afsar Hussain alias Bablu (Dabka village head), Asrar Hussain, Maulana Latif, Irfan Haji, Asif Banda, Zakir and four unknown youths allegedly abducted her. She said they forcibly put her in a car and took her to Chamaraua, where all four uncles beat her with belts, tied her hands and feet, and repeatedly gangraped her. The accused uncle is the caretaker of the mosque where vandalism occurred The woman claimed that the mosque where she created the disturbance belongs to accused uncle Bablu, who is also the village head and mutawalli (caretaker) of the mosque. His house is located right opposite the mosque. Young woman and companion Azeem arrested, court sends them to jail Station House Officer Kuldeep Singh Rana said the woman had earlier named 14 people in serious allegations, including gangrape, kidnapping and property grabbing. The matter is under investigation as per High Court and senior officials’ directions. After returning from court, she reached the mosque in Dabka village and started vandalising it. Despite police presence, she did not stop. A complaint was filed by Dabka resident Mehboob son of Farooq, following which a case was registered against the woman and two others. Both the woman and her associate Azeem were arrested and produced before the SDM court, which sent them to judicial custody. Defence counsel Saurabh Gupta questioned the action, alleging that they were sent to jail without being heard.

stories.title: Tehsildar Rakhi Sharma transferred to Lucknow after action:Commissioner to probe claim of iPhone bribe by Firozabad DM
stories.summary: The Firozabad administration has taken action against Tundla tehsildar Rakhi Sharma (33) and attached her to the Revenue Council headquarters in Lucknow with immediate effect. Rakhi Sharma had levelled serious allegations against Firozabad District Magistrate Ramesh Ranjan, claiming that he had taken a bribe in the form of an iPhone worth ₹1.75 lakh and an Apple Watch. She alleged that she was being harassed and demanded a probe into the matter by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. On Saturday night at 10:17 pm, the District Information Officer informed through the official WhatsApp group that disciplinary proceedings had been initiated against the tehsildar. The government has also ordered a fresh investigation into the disputed land matter, in which allegations of irregularities were made against Kalyan (district treasury) staff. This case was earlier being investigated by Rakhi Sharma. The inquiry has now been assigned to Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant. First understand the entire matter in a sequential manner Rakhi Sharma, originally from Balkeshwar in Agra, has been posted as tehsildar in Tundla since 4 September 2024. She resides in a government guest house. On 16 April, she was transferred from Tundla to Shikohabad tehsil. After the transfer order, she released a video addressed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath alleging harassment by the DM and seeking justice. The following day, on 17 April, she held a press conference in the tehsil premises. Allegations made in press conference Rakhi Sharma alleged that DM Ramesh Ranjan and some officials were harassing her. She named an OSD Shailendra Sharma, a peskar, and a CRA, claiming that these officials formed a group against her. She said a complaint of corruption against these officials was received in July last year and she informed the DM, but instead of action, she was targeted. She alleged that her salary was withheld for eight months and later an adverse entry was issued against her without hearing her side. She further alleged that demands were made for expensive items, including an Apple Watch and an iPhone. She also claimed that the iPhone she had given is still being used by the DM and demanded an investigation into it, saying she has bills and supporting documents. Store kept open late at night for iPhone Rakhi Sharma stated that on 4 November 2025, a showroom in Agra was allegedly kept open late at night on the instructions of the DM’s OSD to arrange an iPhone. She said she was repeatedly pressured to arrange the phone despite not receiving salary. She claimed that after handing over the phone, she was still pressured to keep visiting officials and face humiliation. She also alleged being forced into complying with certain “ethical and unethical orders,” which she said she did not fully comply with. Went to High Court When Salary Didn't Come Rakhi Sharma said she waited for her salary to be released, but when it was not credited, she filed a writ petition in the High Court on 26 February. She alleged that after officials came to know about the petition, her salary was released overnight on 27 February after reopening the treasury. She further claimed that she was called to the camp office and kept confined for two hours, during which she was pressured to withdraw her petition. Had also raised questions about transfer She also questioned her transfer, stating that although she was shifted from Tundla to Shikohabad, she had not received the official transfer letter. Despite this, another tehsildar was posted in her place. The case is also linked to a land dispute from July last year, where complainant Sunayan Sharma alleged irregularities in a 42-bigha land in Usayni. The complaint, filed on the Chief Minister’s portal and at the tehsil office, alleged illegal registration of land in the names of three clerical staff of the collectorate. This matter was under investigation by Rakhi Sharma. Had told Bhaskar - Being threatened for demanding justice Land matter, which will be investigated by the Commissioner Following her allegations, the state government has initiated disciplinary action against Rakhi Sharma and attached her to the Lucknow headquarters. The disputed land case has been ordered for a fresh investigation, now to be conducted by Lucknow Divisional Commissioner Vijay Vishwas Pant.

Trump says US team heading to Pak for talks tomorrow Pakistan has tightened security ahead of possible talks between the US and Iran, with a large number of police and security forces deployed in Islamabad and surrounding areas. 2. He claimed the opposition’s stance has angered women and warned they “will not forgive” them for obstructing political empowerment. 4. Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway cuts journey from 3 hours to 45 minutes Lucknow–Kanpur Expressway cuts travel time from 3 hours to 45 minutes, but toll is nearly three times higher than the highway. stories.title: Akhilesh calls Fatehpur tea seller to SP office:Gifts brass pot; slams raid action and government targeting allegations
stories.summary: The tea seller whose shop was raided in Fatehpur was called to the party office in Lucknow by SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. During the press conference, he said - they are harassing the tea seller. They instigated a leader from the Muslim community to cause an assault, so that a case could be filed. They are conducting raids. The allegation is that tea is being made in aluminum utensils. They are talking about sealing the shop. Whoever is closest to Ajay Singh Bisht, come with me, see, we also have aluminum utensils in our house. Seal my house too. When they didn't spare Shankaracharya, then let's not even talk about others. Actually, the Food Safety Department had raided a tea shop in Fatehpur. They had taken tea samples and sent them for testing. Akhilesh had gone to this shop to drink tea 2 months ago. Because of this, the raid went viral on social media. On this, Akhilesh posted on 'X'. He wrote - Don't be afraid, do your work. Bad days are about to end. Key points of Akhilesh's press conference 1. No right to remain in government Akhilesh said - Today is a very auspicious day. We are from Lucknow. That's why I said, "After you." You have heard a long press conference. You have also heard the TV broadcast. Today we are meeting on the occasion of a historic victory, when the delimitation bill could not be passed. A defeat in Parliament means that the government has lost the trust of the people. It has no right to remain in government. BJP people show fear. They divide society. They serve their own interests. BJP members can do anything to gain and retain power. The BJP's CMF formula (Create, Ministerial, and Fear) has failed. Their tactics will no longer work. The defeat of the BJP has begun. Women will defeat the BJP. Today's new-thinking women will defeat them. 2. Today's woman will not be swayed by them He said - BJP is trying to win over women with old thinking, but today's woman will not be swayed by them. Their thinking about women is feudal. Keep women weak, don't give them rights.. neither of thought, nor of attire. The defeat of the bill brought to divert attention from the growing public opposition, is a defeat for the BJP. They wanted to deceive people. The opposition of the country is representing this victory. 3. It came to usurp women's rights Akhilesh said - In the name of delimitation, it had changed its form to usurp women's rights. This was not a plan to empower women, but to diminish their power. This was not a bill, but a black document of BJP's divisive politics. Even if the population of backward classes is considered 66 percent, women's participation should have been 33 percent. But they were not giving 33 percent reservation to women, they were snatching it. In fact, the very basis of the women's reservation bill was baseless. 4. Such a bill was brought to divert attention He said - Today, there are reports of exploitation of women everywhere. To divert attention from this, such bills are being brought. Our objection was that first a census should be conducted and then reservation should be given. We will not let women be deceived. This is women's appeasement. The concept of 'MP husband' would also have started, just like 'Pradhanpati' (husband of a village head). The government that loses in Parliament goes out. The public has become confident that bad days are going to end. 5. Not reservation, but women should have been made a slogan Akhilesh said - When we came to know last night that a big announcement was going to happen, I thought that a woman's name might come forward for the post of PM. They didn't need reservation; they needed to make women a slogan. Through that, they wanted to deceive us. We also found a video of the head of the current press conference. In it, see what he was saying about the women's reservation bill when he was not in power. That should also be seen. If we are talking about half the population, then everyone should get respect in it. 6. The House was called so that TMC, DMK, Congress people could not campaign He said- Color is associated with some religion or another. Red is the color of revolution as well as our goddesses; the bride's color is also red. The Parliament session was called so that TMC, DMK, Congress people could not campaign, ensuring their security deposits would not be forfeited. On the challenge of former MP Smriti Irani contesting from Gorakhpur, he said that he would change the name of Kannauj to Gorakhpur. He would change the name of Gorakhpur to Gorakhdhanda. Let's understand the full story of the tea shop raid Sheshman Yadav, the owner of a tea shop in Fatehpur, had stated that on Thursday, April 16, Food Safety Department officers and employees came. They took tea samples. They asked, "Why do you make tea in aluminum utensils?" He had alleged that he has been harassed ever since Akhilesh Bhaiya came. Life has been made difficult. If not aluminum, then should we make tea in gold and silver utensils now? Regarding the raid on the tea shop, Food Inspector Dhirendra Dixit had said- A person named Ahmed had filed a complaint on the IGRS portal. He had said that the standards were not being followed in making tea at the shop. Based on that complaint, the team investigated. A tea sample has been taken and sent for testing. Akhilesh had Sheshman's tea, asked - Which leaves do you use? Has any tea shop in Fatehpur been raided before? Has the Food Safety Department in Fatehpur raided any tea shop before this? When the department's officials were asked about this, they said they would be able to tell after checking. However, department sources say that no tea shop in the district has been raided before. The department mostly conducts raids on sweet shops or restaurants. Action will be taken after the investigation report Food Inspector Dhirendra Dixit says- After the sample report comes, further action will be taken. If the standards are not met, the shop can also be sealed. Currently, the investigation is ongoing.

stories.title: 150-year-old market in Firozabad engulfed in huge fire:More than 60 shops gutted; cash worth lakhs turns to ash
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in Firozabad's 150-year-old vegetable market, reducing more than 60 shops to ashes. Seven other shops, including a garment store located in front of the market, were also engulfed in flames. By the time people were informed of the incident late at night, most of the shops had already burned down. Six fire engines that arrived after receiving information brought the fire under control after nearly four hours of effort. This incident occurred on Saturday in Katra Bazaar of Shikohabad. The cause of the fire has not yet been determined. However, preliminary investigation suggests short circuit as a possible reason. Revenue and Fire Department teams are assessing the damage. Visuals of the fire How the incident occured There is a 150-year-old vegetable market in Katra Bazaar of Shikoabad. There are 60 shops in the market. This is the largest fruit and vegetable market in the city. Business worth lakhs takes place here daily. On Saturday late night around 2 am, a fire broke out in a shop due to some reasons. Within moments, the fire spread throughout the entire market. Before local people could get information, the flames engulfed the entire market. The fire was so horrific that flames were rising 10 feet high in the sky. The flames and clouds of smoke could be seen from several kilometers away. The fire from the vegetable market spread to another nearby market. Fire spread to seven shops there. In no time, a garment shop along with 6 other shops were also burnt to ashes. When information about the fire in the market was received, shopkeepers and people from nearby areas arrived. The fire brigade was informed. People from Shikohabad fire brigade reached the spot. However, seeing the severity of the fire, fire brigade vehicles from surrounding areas were also called. After this, 6 fire brigade vehicles brought the fire under control after 4 hours of work. Lakhs of rupees in cash burnt along with goods Mohammad Sail, who runs a shop in the market, said, 'There is a huge stock of vegetables in the market. There would hardly be any shop that doesn't have 20 thousand to 50 thousand rupees in its cash box. Everything turned to ash in the fire. Our earnings from years of hard work were destroyed in a moment.' Shopkeeper Munnalal said, ‘There are about 60 vegetable and fruit shops in the market. There are also 7 cloth shops adjacent to each other in the market. Both markets were burnt to ashes. We traders have suffered losses worth crores. Even the dog living in the market cannot be traced.’ Chief Fire Officer Satyendra Pandey said, ‘The team reached the spot as soon as information about the fire was received. Most of the shops in the market are vegetable and clothing stores. This number is around 50-60. The cause of the fire has not yet been determined. However, it appears that it happened due to a short circuit.’

stories.title: 'INDI alliance opposing Women's Reservation Bill was like Draupadi's disrobing':CM Yogi attacks SP, Cong; says half the population won't forgive them
stories.summary: CM Yogi held a press conference in Lucknow on Sunday with BJP and allied parties. During this, he took a dig at SP-Congress regarding the Women's Reservation Amendment Bill in Parliament. Yogi said, ‘There are 78 women MPs in Parliament. PM Modi wanted to increase this, but Congress-SP became barriers. SP had an opportunity to wash away the sins of the guest house scandal. They want everything to go to their family. They opposed the bill so that no other woman gets it.’ He said, 'The Nari Shakti Vandan Act was approved in 2023. The Nari Shakti Vandan Amendment Bill was brought to implement it from 2029. A special session was called. PM Modi had said that no one's rights will be taken away. Seats will be increased in Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha.' He added, 'PM assured the southern states that their rights will not be reduced. The entire House should unite and give Nari Shakti their rights from 2029, but the behavior of the INDIA alliance in the House was like Draupadi's disrobing. What kind of language was used.' Yogi stated, There is anger among the women power of UP against SP and Congress. SP and Congress should apologize to half the population. Half the population is not going to forgive them. This is unforgivable. The INDI alliance has become an obstacle among women's leadership. The women power of India will not accept this. Yogi's big statements 1. Anger Due to Opposition's Anti-Women Conduct Yogi said - The entire country has witnessed the conduct of Indi Alliance parties during the Nari Shakti Vandan Amendment Bill. As soon as Modi took charge of the country's power, he had said that there are only four castes in the country - women, poor, youth and farmers. For those who looted the country to feed their families with the intention of weakening India, this was a challenge. Congress and its allied parties opposed every progressive step. There is immense anger in the minds of half the population due to the opposition's anti-women conduct. 2. SP Talked About Reservation for Muslim Women Yogi said - The Indi Alliance conspires. If the bill had been passed, Nari Shakti would have got rights. SP talked about reservation for Muslim women. SP people invoke the Constitution, but Baba Saheb had opposed reservation on the basis of religion. He had said that India cannot endure partition repeatedly, but SP demanded reservation for Muslim women. Where were the SP people when Congress snatched away the rights of Muslim women in the Shah Bano case, the INDIA alliance also opposed the Triple Talaq law. This shows their double standards. Congress and the INDIA alliance got the opportunity to rule the country for the longest time, but they did not take any steps for women, farmers, youth and the poor. 3. The government implemented several schemes for women empowerment Yogi said - In efforts for women power, the first proposal of Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was passed. The double engine government has made arrangements for the daughter's education from her birth. 26 lakh daughters have benefited. The government has implemented many schemes for women empowerment. Women have benefited from this. This has brought transformation in women's lives. Women have been advanced in all fields including education, health and defense. stories.title: 'My height increased by 5 cm, head was swollen':Astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla shares secrets of space travel
stories.summary: Indian Air Force Group Captain and Astronaut Shubhanshu Shukla has revealed another secret from his space journey. He has shared information about the changes that occurred in his body during that time. He said that his height increased by 5 cm there and his head became swollen. He shared this on Thursday at the Summer Plant Science Festival organized at NBRI in Lucknow. Shubhanshu said, ‘There was no gravitational force in space. Due to this, the heart was pumping blood upwards. This caused blood to accumulate towards the head, which was increasing the swelling in the head. The heart was shrinking, muscle mass was decreasing. Not only this, his height also increased by up to 5 centimeters. My body returned to normal 15 days after returning to Earth.’ ‘Earth is priceless, even wood is like diamonds’ Shubhanshu Shukla said that Earth looks extremely beautiful when viewed from space. Whatever is here is not only priceless but also extremely rare. That's why Earth is the most precious in the entire universe. The wood found here will not be found anywhere else in the entire space. It will be found only here, meaning wood is as precious as diamonds for other planets. It is very necessary to preserve the Earth for its beauty and the preciousness of life on it, it is necessary to stop the increasing pollution here. This is only possible when a global perspective is adopted for this. Along with this, he said that only new technology is not sufficient for Earth conservation. Discipline and strict laws are also necessary for this. 'India is growing faster than the speed of thought' During this time, Shubhanshu said that India is rapidly touching new heights in the field of space science and is moving forward at a faster pace than the world's expectations. Soon the country will have its own space station established in space. It is hoped that by 2035 we will be able to work independently on that station. Praises India's constitution for promoting scientific temper Shubhanshu mentioned that India's Constitution is the only constitution in the world that considers developing scientific temper among its citizens as a fundamental duty. While sharing his space travel experiences, he talked about experiments conducted on cyanobacteria and algae in microgravity at the International Space Station. He also narrated several interesting incidents.

stories.title: Noida violence mastermind had full data of workers:Joined labour groups 5 years ago; gathered crowd through WhatsApp
stories.summary: Aditya Anand, the main conspirator of the violent workers' movement in Noida, had been preparing for this for five years. He read about 'Mazdoor Bigul' on Facebook. He joined it in 2022. He came in contact with Mazdoor Bigul's editor Anubhav Sinha and started reporting on incidents happening in Noida's factories. During this time, he met Rupesh Rai, the head of a workers' organization. Rupesh also started going on reporting assignments with Aditya. Both of them created complete data of Noida's industry. What is the situation, what can be done? With this data, between March 30 and April 1, people from five organizations - Mazdoor Bigul, Disha Sangathan, RWPI, Naujawan Bharat Sabha and Ekta Sangharsh Samiti - gathered in a room in Arun Vihar, Sector-37, Noida. Software Engineer Aditya gathered crowd through WhatsApp Additional Superintendent of Police (STF) Rajkumar Mishra said- Planning was done at Aditya Anand's house for three days. Preparations were made on how to make Noida's industry and workers violent. Under the guise of a labor movement, a plan was made for violence, arson and damaging public property. After making the plan, these people created WhatsApp groups between 9th and 10th April. Aditya is a software engineer. Therefore, technology was used. STF nabbed from Tiruchirappalli Railway Station A non-bailable warrant (NBW) was issued against Aditya. There was a reward of one lakh on him. As soon as he got the information, he went straight from Noida to Chennai. Meanwhile, police teams were continuously conducting raids in several states to catch him. They were taking help of surveillance. During this time, he was going from Chennai to Tiruchirappalli. But, STF got wind of it. The Noida unit of STF arrested him from the station itself. Know about Aditya Anand When and how the Noida violence occured

stories.title: Akhilesh gave Smriti an opportunity by calling her 'saas-bahu wali':Sidelined after losing Amethi, will TV's 'Tulsi' make a comeback?
stories.summary: As soon as Akhilesh Yadav said in Parliament - that 'saas-bahu wali' lost, laughter echoed in the house. Smriti Irani was the target. After losing the Lok Sabha election from Amethi, Smriti may have been less visible in active politics, but she made a comeback in the TV world. Her show 'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi' is in the news again with a new season. Smriti, who once defeated Rahul Gandhi, is now not seen in Amethi. In such a situation, the question arises - Will TV's 'Tulsi' make a comeback again? Has the Amethi defeat become a turning point in her career? Why did Akhilesh take her name in Parliament? Know about Smriti Irani in today's Sunday Big Story... Family with Political Background Father a Congress member, Mother in BJP Smriti was born in a middle-class family in Delhi. Her father Ajay Kumar Malhotra was from Punjabi and Maharashtrian background. Her mother Shibani Bagchi was from a Bengali family. This is why Smriti had a strong grip on Punjabi, Marathi and Bengali languages since childhood. Her father was a Congress member, but her mother was active in BJP. Her grandfather was also a volunteer of the Sangh. Smriti was more influenced by her mother and grandfather. Benefited from the Identity of a Cultured Daughter-in-law After completing her schooling, Smriti became active in the TV world. In the year 2000, she appeared in the serials 'Aatish' and 'Hum Hain Kal Aaj Aur Kal'. However, she gained recognition from the serial 'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi'. By 2002, this serial started being watched in every household. This was the time when Smriti began to be recognized not by her real name, but by her serial character name 'Tulsi'. Entry into Politics Fought first election from Delhi Smriti had become popular across the country. This was the time when she stepped into politics. In 2003, she took membership of the BJP. Her influence in the party grew so rapidly that in 2004 she was made the Vice President of Maharashtra BJP Yuva Morcha. Since Smriti was a resident of Delhi, she fought her first election from the Chandni Chowk seat in 2004. She had to face defeat at the hands of Congress's Kapil Sibal. Became National President of Mahila Morcha From 2004 to 2010, the BJP was not in power at the center, but Smriti continued to promote the party. In 2008, the serial 'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi' ended. However, Smriti's identity as a cultured daughter-in-law had reached every household. Now she became more active in Gujarat and Maharashtra. She benefited from this in 2010. She was made the National President of BJP Mahila Morcha. In 2011, the party sent her to Rajya Sabha from Gujarat. After this, Smriti Irani started appearing in a different avatar. She remained constantly aggressive towards Congress. Especially, she was seen making statements about Rahul Gandhi. Stature grew in politics Lost to Rahul Gandhi, Yet Became a Cabinet Minister This is why when the 2014 Lok Sabha elections came, Smriti was sent to contest from Congress's traditional seat Amethi. Rahul Gandhi had already been elected MP from here twice. In 2014, BJP formed the government at the center, but Smriti lost against Rahul Gandhi. Even after losing, Smriti came into the limelight. Actually, in 2009, Rahul won the election by a margin of 3.70 lakh votes. However, against Smriti, this margin reduced to 1.07 lakh. This was the reason why despite losing the election, Smriti was made a Cabinet Minister. Even after losing to Rahul Gandhi, Smriti remained active in Amethi. She started staying there intermittently. She would visit workers' homes, meet them, and help them. When the 2019 Lok Sabha elections came, Smriti turned history around. Rahul Gandhi lost the election. Smriti Irani received 4 lakh 68 thousand votes. She secured victory by 55 thousand votes. This victory greatly elevated Smriti's stature. She was made the Minister of Women and Child Development in the central government. Lost Election in 2024 Came to Amethi only once In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Smriti staked her claim from Amethi again. This time, not Rahul Gandhi from Congress, but Kishori Lal Sharma, who had been his MP representative, entered the fray. He defeated Smriti Irani by 1.67 lakh votes. After this defeat, Smriti Irani went to Amethi only once. On May 26, 2025, she went to Amethi on Ahilyabai Holkar Jayanti. She met with party workers there. She has not gone there again since then. Praveen Kumar Singh, District Vice President of BJP in Amethi, says - Smriti Didi's team is working in Amethi. She remains in constant contact with everyone. She keeps getting information about what is happening. Her attachment to Amethi has not diminished. She is still campaigning for BJP in different states. She will contest elections from Amethi again in the future. Became active in TV again Became famous from Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Season-2 Smriti is neither an MP now nor in the government. She has not been given any position in the organization either. Smriti continued to work for the party like a worker. Her activity in the party was not visible as before. This time also became a turning point in her life. Smriti moved from politics towards TV. On July 29, 2025, Smriti was once again seen on TV in the famous character of 'Tulsi Virani'. This was the second season of 'Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi'. Once again, she began to be watched in every household in the role of a woman standing up against values and challenges. The popularity of this serial can be understood from the fact that it is among the top-3 shows on Star Plus. It has a TRP of 3.2 and is trending at number 1 in the list of 'Most Watched' shows on OTT Jio Hotstar. BJP made her a star campaigner in Bengal elections Smriti once again benefited from TV popularity. BJP made her a star campaigner in the Bengal Assembly elections. She is doing rallies and road shows for BJP candidates. She is able to connect directly with the public by giving speeches in Bengali. She is famous among the public, especially among women. Before this, the party had also made Smriti a star campaigner in Bihar. However, she was not in the list of star campaigners in the Maharashtra elections. Says, ‘Focus on Parliament, not serials’ A discussion was underway in the Lok Sabha on a constitutional amendment bill to implement women's reservation. On April 16, Akhilesh Yadav said in Parliament - If seats are reserved for women, then competition among women will increase. A voice came from BJP MPs - That should happen. Akhilesh said laughingly - Your 'saas-bahu wali' lost... Here Akhilesh's reference to 'saas-bahu wali' was to Smriti Irani. 1.30 hours after this comment, Smriti responded. She wrote in a social media post: "I heard that Akhilesh ji remembered me in Parliament today...That's good. Those who got politics as inheritance also remember those who make holes in the sky on their own strength. They comment on working women who have never done any job in their life. Shift focus from serials to Parliament. Get the important bill passed for women's support." The next day, i.e., on April 17, Akhilesh Yadav posted a shayari on social media. He wrote, "If every matter hadn't reeked of conspiracy, People would have believed if the talk hadn't been mere rhetoric, Actually, if friendship with the public had been maintained, Then the moment of farewell wouldn't have arrived so soon." Smriti said, ‘Their staying in opposition is certain’ On April 17, Smriti Irani reached Varanasi. There she said, ‘A working woman like me went to Congress stronghold Amethi and defeated the National President. If you have so much courage, then leave your ancestral seat and contest from Gorakhpur and show us.’ She said, ‘It is easy to comment on women like us, especially for those who have never done any job. We people pay taxes, not so that saas-bahu (mother-in-law daughter-in-law) matters are discussed inside the Lok Sabha. One should go to Parliament and focus on their parliamentary work.’ 'I am happy that their staying in opposition in UP is certain, because those who do politics in UP spend so much time roaming village to village that a serious leader doesn't get time to watch serials,' she added. What do the people of Amethi say? 'Smriti's team is active, the public is remembering them' We spoke to many people in Amethi regarding Smriti Irani's activeness. Senior journalist Vindeshwari Mishra says - the people of Amethi are remembering Smriti Irani. The main reason for this is that the expectations with which the public elected Kishori Lal Sharma in 2024, he has not lived up to them. The public is recalling the tenure from 2019 to 2024. Smriti used to continuously work here for development.

stories.title: Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway cuts journey from 3 hours to 45 minutes:Toll 3 times higher than highway; may be inaugurated next month
stories.summary: The Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway is ready and complete. It is among UP's shortest expressways, but travellers will have to pay 3 times the toll as compared to the National Highway on it. Now the journey from Lucknow to Kanpur will be completed in just 45 minutes instead of 3 hours. Vehicles will be able to run at a speed of 120 km on the high-speed expressway. However, only cars and vans are allowed to run, bikes will not be permitted. Of the 63 km long expressway, 18 km is elevated (road built on pillars). CCTV cameras installed for surveillance can see up to a range of 500 meters. Facilities like fuel stations, restaurants, trauma centers and parking are being built along the way for travellers. Toll tax boards have also been installed. It is being said that its inauguration will also take place next month. In such a situation, will people get those facilities? To see this, Bhaskar's team traveled on the expressway. How accurate are the claims are? Read the report… Traffic started running till Banthra before inauguration Our team reached National Highway-27. We proceeded from Lucknow towards Chaudhary Charan Singh Airport (Amausi). There was a traffic jam on the main road. Passing through this, we reached Sarojininagar. From here we tried to climb onto the elevated bridge. We saw that stones were placed blocking the road. However, one section was open. Bikers were going onto the expressway from here. Actually, the expressway is closed for common people. However, people have started using it till Banthra. After talking to NHAI officials, we took permission for coverage of the entire expressway. After this, we got onto the expressway. After travelling about 3-4 km, we saw Scooter India (old factory). At this point, the road was elevated. We looked down below. On National Highway-27, where there used to be traffic jams, people were now able to drive their vehicles comfortably. Service lanes y for Outer Ring Road After going a little further, the elevated road descended downwards, because ahead is the Lucknow Outer Ring Road. If someone comes from Kanpur and needs to go to Raebareli, Sitapur, Hardoi, Sultanpur, they won't need to enter Lucknow city. They can pass through this route. The Outer Ring Road is built in an area of about 105 km. Service roads have been constructed here for getting on and off the Ring Road. Transmission lines are passing through monopoles After travelling 12 km on the expressway, we reached Gauri Chauraha in Banthra. It was found that this section took the longest time to build the expressway. Actually, 1.32 lakh volt transmission lines pass through here. To shift them, 3 monopoles needed to be built. After the monopoles were built, they were sent to Hyderabad for testing. Only 2 monopoles passed the testing. The third monopole had to be built again. After passing the testing, it was brought to Lucknow. Only then could the transmission lines be shifted. After that, the expressway could be built here. The expressway and highway separated at Bani spot Most of the expressway passing through Lucknow is elevated. The reason for this is that the National Highway exists below. From Amausi to Darogakheda, the expressway is 4 lanes. Beyond this, from Bani (name of the place), the expressway and highway separate. This expressway is built in a greenland area. Meaning there was no road here before. It goes through the villages of Datauli, Kantha, Taura, Nerona in Unnao district up to Amarsaas. Our vehicle went over these villages. The construction of the road has been completed. Will have to pay 3 times more toll A total of 4 toll plazas have been built on the entire expressway. If you travel by car, the one-way toll will be 275 rupees. If you return within 24 hours, the total toll will be 410 rupees. Currently, to reach Kanpur from the highway, one has to go through the Nawabganj toll plaza. The car toll on the highway is 95 rupees. This means you will have to pay three times more toll to travel on the expressway instead of the highway. Restaurants and fuel stations to be built There are plans to provide facilities like fuel stations, restaurants, trauma centers and parking on the expressway. While passing through Unnao, we found several empty spots along the road. Officials from NHAI informed that restaurants and fuel stations are to be built at different spots. Meanwhile, the trauma centre will be built near the toll plaza. According to officials, their construction will be carried out after the inauguration. For now, Rest and Service boards have been installed on the expressway. Why is the Expressway special? High-tech cameras While travelling on the Expressway, CCTVs are visible every 1 km. NHAI officials said that 63 CCTVs have been installed on the entire Expressway. These cameras are so powerful that they can see clearly up to 500 meters. The zooming power is good. They can move upwards and downwards. 6 Interchanges As many as six interchanges have been built at different locations on the road. People can enter and exit the expressway from here. The main toll spot is located after Shaheed Path. Then two spots have been built in Lucknow itself and in Harauni. The remaining two have been built in Unnao at Ajgain and Amarsaas. Then the main toll is at Azad Chowk in Kanpur. Online challan 21 CCTVs have been installed for surveillance at the interchanges. Officials claim that those coming on the road from the wrong direction will be challaned by monitoring these cameras. Accident alert The expressway is also special because 16 VIDS (Video Incident Detection System) cameras have been installed to alert about accidents, fires and stationary vehicles. These cameras are equipped with AI. They will send messages to the control room. Help will be sent from there. Control Room management Two control rooms have been built on this road. First at 27 km. Second at 35 km. Monitoring will be done from here. Union Road and Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari claims that people can reach from Lucknow to Kanpur in 45 minutes. However, this doesn't seem to be happening. Underpasses, 6 flyovers, 28 small bridges built on links Underpasses were built where there were link roads on the expressway. 38 such underpasses were seen. 6 flyovers, 3 large and 28 small bridges have been constructed, so that vehicles can run at high speed (120 km). Until now, people used to rely on National Highway-27 to go from Lucknow to Kanpur. The distance between both cities via the highway is 93 km. After the road, people only had the option of train. The distance between the two cities by train is 74 km. The journey by train takes 2 hours. Direct flights have not been started between Lucknow-Kanpur. There are connecting flights, but the travel cost reaches up to 7 to 8 thousand rupees. Why the Lucknow-Kanpur expressway had to be built There used to be traffic jam situations on the Lucknow-Kanpur highway. Keeping this in view, it was decided that an expressway should be built between the two cities. In November 2018, the Detailed Project Report (DPR) of this project was submitted to the UP government, but the work stopped due to Corona. Land acquisition was completed between September 2020 and February 2021. Farmers were given approximately 900 crore rupees as compensation. Construction began in April 2021. It passes through 11 villages of Lucknow and 31 villages of Unnao district. Why is it called the most expensive expressway? According to NHAI officials, 4700 crore rupees were spent to build the 62.7 km long road. That means approximately 75 crore rupees were spent to build 1 km of road. The 594 km long Ganga Expressway was built at a cost of 37 thousand 350 crore rupees. That means approximately 63 crore rupees were spent per km. Thus, this will be the most expensive expressway so far. The reason for this is the higher circle rates of land here. Farmers were given 900 crore rupees just as compensation. Economic impact
