stories.title: Father slits throats of 11-year-old twin daughters in Kanpur:Accused calls police himself; motive for murder yet to be uncovered
stories.summary: On early Sunday morning in Kanpur, a man murdered his 11-year-old twin daughters. The father slit their throats inside the flat and then informed the police himself. He has been arrested. DCP South Deependra Nath Chaudhary said that the accused, Shashi Ranjan Mishra, a medical representative, lived in Trimurti Apartment in Kidwai Nagar under the Naubasta police station area. He lived with his wife Reshma Kshetri and their three children, 11-year-old twin daughters Riddhi and Siddhi, and a 6-year-old son, Gannu. Around 4:30 am on Sunday, police received information about the murders via the emergency number 112. When police reached the flat, both girls’ bodies were found lying side by side on the floor. The entire room was covered in blood. Their throats had been slit, and a knife was found nearby. The accused father was sitting next to the bodies and was arrested on the spot. The motive behind the killings is not yet known. Wife demands death penalty for husband Crying, the wife Reshma said that her husband should be given the death penalty immediately. She stated that they had a love marriage in 2014, but he would beat her daily under the influence of alcohol. He had installed CCTV cameras from the entrance to the kitchen and bedroom and would not allow her to enter the room. He stayed inside with the two daughters, and she could only watch the room’s footage on a screen from outside. He would often tell her to leave with their son, saying he would raise the daughters himself. Husband used to get drunk and beat wife Reshma said, “I am from Siliguri, Bengal. My husband is from Bihar. I worked at a men's parlor in Kanpur. During that time, I met Shashi Ranjan Mishra. We had a love marriage in 2014. The relationship deteriorated after the wedding. He wouldn't let me go to my parents' house. He would always come home drunk and beat me. He always told me to go away with my son and that he would take care of both our daughters.' She said, 'If I went out, they wouldn't even let me come back home. I went to my parents' house with my son. They wouldn't let me take my daughters with me. Then, I couldn't bear to be without my daughters, and returned to my in-laws' house after about nine months. My husband always said, "My mother is dead. Now I want to die too. I'll take both our daughters with me. You raise your son.' She said, 'My husband used to take sleeping pills along with alcohol. I don't know what he was doing. He wouldn't let anyone into his room. When he went out, we would go into the room.' Went to sleep with daughters at 2.30 am in the night The wife said, ‘Everything was fine last night. He ate dinner and went to sleep with his daughters. He spoke to someone on the phone for a long time. I was watching everything in his room on the camera screen outside. Around 2:30 am in the night, he took his daughter to the washroom. Then, after a while, he took his daughter back to his room. He turned off the lights.’ 'Then I went to the door and windows of his room and listened, but I heard no movement or sound. I assumed everyone was asleep. After that, I don't know when the murder took place.'

stories.title: Heatwave alert in 6 cities of UP, temperatures cross 40°C:IMD advises people to stay indoors
stories.summary: Severe heat is prevailing in UP. The temperature in 26 districts has reached 40C or more. Bright sunshine emerged in most districts from morning on Sunday. Due to low wind speed, humidity is being felt. The roads are deserted. Talking about the last 24 hours, Banda was the third hottest city in the country. The maximum temperature was recorded at 44.6C. A day earlier, that is on Friday, Banda was the hottest city in Asia. Then the maximum temperature was recorded at 45.4C. This time, the heat has started showing its effect about 10 days earlier than normal. Last year, the temperature crossed 45C for the first time on April 27, whereas this time this situation has occurred in mid-April itself. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a heat-wave alert today in Banda, Chitrakoot, Kaushambi, Prayagraj and nearby districts of eastern UP. People have been advised to stay indoors and go out during afternoon only if absolutely necessary. Lucknow meteorological scientist Atul Singh said- Due to the effect of the anti-cyclone formed around Maharashtra, there will be an increase of 2-3C in temperature during the next 2-3 days. The temperature of most districts will reach 45C or above. There is a possibility of heat waves in some places in eastern UP. Currently, there is no hope of relief from the heat in the remaining days of April. 3-day heat wave warning in UP Heatwave may persist for a long time According to IMD's forecast, heatwave conditions may persist for a long time in some areas this year. This means that temperatures may remain very high for several consecutive days in many cities and people may have to face intense heat. When is it considered a heatwave? According to the Meteorological Department, a heatwave is considered when the temperature in plains reaches 40 degrees Celsius or more, or when the temperature is recorded 4 to 6 degrees above normal. In such conditions, people's health can also be affected and the risk of heatstroke increases. What are El-Nio and La-Nia? Does cold food mean 'cold things kept in the fridge'? No, 'cooling food' means those that keep the body cool from inside and have a cooling nature. For example- Foods like watermelon, cucumber, bottle gourd, curd and buttermilk have a cooling nature. They keep the body hydrated and help in balancing body temperature. Whereas cold drinks, cold coffee or very cold water from the fridge provide coolness for a few minutes, but they do not cool the body from inside.

stories.title: Man falls into stubble fire after bike hits truck, dies:Dense smoke from burning fields causes crash on Deoria road; child rescued by passerby
stories.summary: A 40-year-old man died after his bike rammed into a truck and he fell into a burning stubble fire on the roadside. He remained trapped in the flames for nearly 30 minutes and died on the spot. The incident took place around 4 pm on Saturday. The victim, Musafir, a labourer who worked in Pune, was going to his sister’s house in Isharpura for a family wedding. He lived in Birwa village under Gauri Bazar police station with his wife Sunita and three children—Tinku (11), Kajal (8) and Chhotu (6). Now know the complete matter... Smoke from burning fields led to accident The accident happened on the Rudrapur-Pachladi road near Kashipur village. Stubble had been burnt across more than 100 acres of fields. Thick smoke covered the entire road, reducing visibility to near zero. Musafir was passing through the smoke when he failed to see a truck moving ahead. His bike crashed into the vehicle from behind. Due to the impact, he fell into bushes on the roadside that were already on fire. Severely injured, he could not get up and remained trapped in the flames. Locals rushed to help and tried to douse the fire by pouring water with buckets, but could not save him. Son survives, rescued by another biker Musafir’s six-year-old son Chhotu, who was riding with him, fell on the other side of the road during the collision. This saved his life. At the same time, another biker coming from behind also slipped due to the heavy smoke. His bike too caught fire after falling into the burning area. However, he managed to get up and noticed the child lying nearby. He quickly picked him up and moved him to safety on the roadside. Fire brought under control, bikes seized Police and fire brigade teams reached the spot and brought the fire under control. Musafir’s body was later sent for postmortem. Both burnt bikes have been seized. The injured child was taken to Rudrapur Health Centre for treatment. The incident highlights the danger posed by stubble burning, especially when thick smoke reduces visibility on busy roads.

Similarly, girls from Mandhana 1 Composite, Mandhana 2 Composite, Horabangar, Kursauli Composite, Upper Primary School Katri, Shankarpur, Upper Primary School Gambhirpur Kachhar, and Bhajanlal Swatantra Sangram Inter College, Gabardha, among other places, were also given the final vaccine dose free of cost. The vaccination drive was conducted by the team from the Community Medicine Department of GSVM Medical College. The campaign will continue regularly, along with spreading awareness and providing guidance on cancer prevention. The objective of the campaign is to protect people from cancer and ensure maximum awareness reaches the public. Health centre staff, including Nurse Usha and Dr. Anurag Mishra, played a key role in the drive. The campaign was coordinated by Dr. Praveen Katiyar, with significant support from volunteers Manish, Kritika, Mansi, Kumud, Sagar, Pratik Patel, Pratik Maurya, Tanya, Harshit Gangwar, Adnan, Manmendra, and others.

stories.title: Cyber security conference concludes at Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University:Online and offline participants awarded, experts share insights
stories.summary: A two-day international conference on “Cyber Security Law and Administration: Building Global Resilience” concluded on Saturday at Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University (CSJMU). The event was hosted by the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Legal Studies and brought together academicians, researchers and experts to discuss emerging cyber challenges. The conference was organised under the guidance of Vice-Chancellor Prof. Vinay Kumar Pathak and the patronage of Director Dr. Smriti Roy. Dr. Shashikant Tripathi served as president, Dr. Rahul Tiwari as co-president, while Dr. Smriti Roy and Dr. Divyansh Shukla coordinated the event. Kaushiki Trivedi and Vidhi Katiyar were co-coordinators. The second day began with registrations, followed by a series of technical sessions held in both online and offline formats. Experts led in-depth discussions on cyber security, cyber governance, artificial intelligence, and cybercrime. Research scholars presented papers during offline sessions, receiving guidance and feedback from senior academicians. The valedictory session took place at the Senanayak Tatya Tope Senate Hall, starting with the traditional lamp lighting ceremony. Kaushiki Trivedi presented a summary of the conference proceedings. Keynote speakers addressed issues related to cyber law, governance and global digital threats. Prof. J.P. Rai emphasised the growing challenges in cyber governance and the need for international cooperation. During the closing ceremony, outstanding research paper presenters were honoured across multiple sessions. Awards were given to participants for excellence in both online and offline categories. Dr. Sammuddin summarised the conference outcomes and expressed gratitude to all contributors. Certificates were distributed to researchers, while faculty members and volunteers were also recognised for their efforts. With engaging sessions, insightful discussions and active participation, the international conference concluded successfully.

stories.title: High-profile Kanpur rave busted:140 youths, IIT students among those intoxicated
stories.summary: Police raided a high-profile rave party late Friday night in the city and found around 140 youths, including students from reputed institutes such as IIT, in an intoxicated state. Many of those present were from Kanpur, while others had come from Delhi, Haryana and Rajasthan. The party was being held at Stella Naomi Club in NRI City under the name ‘Sonic Shift’. Police said several drugs were recovered from the spot, including LSD, cocaine, marijuana, charas and hashish. The organiser and the alleged drug supplier have been arrested and sent to jail. Police said the party was organised through invitations sent on Instagram. Acting on a tip-off about drug use, the Special Operations Group (SOG) launched a covert operation under “Operation White Powder”, which is being led by trainee IPS officer Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke. Undercover entry, late-night raid According to Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal, two police personnel entered the party after purchasing passes worth ₹1,000. Around 2:30 am, when most attendees were under the influence of drugs and alcohol, the undercover team alerted backup units. A raid was then carried out. As police entered, panic broke out inside the club and many tried to flee. However, the main gate was shut, preventing escape. Police detained those present and later released most of them after issuing warnings. Organiser, supplier arrested The organiser was identified as Mohammad Fardeen alias Gumti, a resident of Jajmau, while the alleged drug supplier, Mohit Jaiswal, lives near Sant Nagar Chowraha. Police said Jaiswal had brought LSD from Pushkar in Rajasthan to sell at the party. Investigators said drugs were being distributed among partygoers, and large LED screens and projectors were installed to enhance the psychedelic effects. Drugs and cash recovered Police recovered small quantities of multiple narcotics, including LSD, marijuana, charas, cocaine and hashish. They also seized smoking equipment and ₹49,000 in cash from the venue. Officials said further raids are being conducted at other clubs in the city as part of the ongoing crackdown on narcotics. What is LSD? LSD (Lysergic Acid Diethylamide) is a powerful hallucinogenic drug that affects the brain and alters perception. After consumption, users may see or hear things that are not real, a condition often described as a “trip”. Its effects usually begin within 15 to 30 minutes and can last for several hours. During this period, colours, lights and sounds appear more intense, and users may feel strongly drawn to music and visual effects.

stories.title: Trader suffers heart attack during anti-encroachment drive, dies:Action by Lucknow Municipal Corporation outside shops; panic after demolition
stories.summary: A businessman died suddenly during an anti-encroachment drive by the Lucknow Municipal Corporation in Rajajipuram’s E Block on Saturday, triggering tension in the area. According to reports, the civic team had reached the locality to remove illegal encroachments. As the drive began, the businessman present at the spot protested. During the argument, his health suddenly worsened and he collapsed. Eyewitnesses said he was rushed towards a nearby hospital, but he had stopped breathing by then. The municipal team had demolished a shop in the same area during the operation. Soon after the incident, a large number of traders gathered in the market, leading to a tense situation. Additional Municipal Commissioner Arun Kumar Gupta said the drive continued peacefully till around 3:30 pm and no untoward incident occurred during the action. He added that the traders’ association of Rajajipuram E Block had itself requested the corporation to remove encroachments. Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar also denied any link between the civic action and the trader’s death, calling such claims rumours. However, the deceased’s family has alleged that he suffered a heart attack due to stress caused by the demolition drive. Police have sent the body for post-mortem, and an investigation is underway. The situation in the area remains tense. Further updates are awaited.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. Centre approves 2% DA hike for central govt employees, pensioners The Union Cabinet on Saturday, April 18, approved a 2% hike in Dearness Allowance (DA) for central government employees and pensioners, raising it from 58% to 60% of basic pay. The revision, effective from January 2026, will also apply to pensioners through a corresponding increase in Dearness Relief (DR), leading to higher monthly payouts. 2. Yogi asks Mamata to vacate West Bengal throne, targets TMC rule Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath urged Mamata Banerjee to step down, claiming BJP will form government in West Bengal. He accused TMC of backing infiltrators and vowed to end “love jihad”, as “Bulldozer Baba” slogans echoed at a Mathabhanga rally. 3. Aparna Yadav protests over women’s bill setback, burns SP-Congress flags In Lucknow, BJP leader Aparna Yadav staged a late-night protest over the Women’s Reservation Bill setback, burning SP and Congress flags. She accused the opposition of blocking women’s rights, calling them “pretentious” and warning that “Nari Shakti” will respond strongly. 4. Iran reimposes restrictions on Hormuz over US blockade on ports Iran's IRGC has issued a statement claiming that control of the Strait of Hormuz has now “returned to its previous state” due to the US’s continuing blockade of Iranian ports. In a statement cited by Iran’s IRIB broadcaster, the IRGC command said the US has “continued acts of piracy and maritime theft under the guise of a so-called blockade”. 5. Stay on FIR against Rahul Gandhi: Allahabad High Court flags no-notice lapse, halts action Stay on FIR order against Rahul Gandhi: Allahabad High Court revisits directive, flags lack of prior notice as legally untenable; Justice Subhash Vidyarthi halts action in alleged dual citizenship case, orders fresh hearing on April 20, petitioner plans move to Supreme Court against rollback decision. 6. She claimed sustained pressure over complaints and has sought intervention from Yogi Adityanath for justice. 7. NDA women MPs protest over Women's Reservation Bill defeat NDA leaders are protesting nationwide over the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill not passing in the Lok Sabha. stories.title: Varanasi ₹40 lakh jewellery theft busted:Two ₹25,000-reward thieves arrested after scanning 250+ CCTV clips
stories.summary: The Varanasi Police Commissionerate has arrested two accused involved in a major house theft and recovered jewellery worth around ₹40 lakh, officials said. The incident took place in Gayatri Nagar under the Lanka Police Station Varanasi area. The victim’s family had gone to their native village on March 31, 2026. When they returned on April 4, they found the lock of their house broken and ancestral jewellery along with other valuables missing. Police registered a case and launched an investigation soon after receiving the complaint. Case cracked using CCTV footage During the probe, police scanned more than 250 CCTV camera recordings from the area. Based on this extensive surveillance, the suspects were identified. Investigators found that the accused used to roam in residential areas posing as street vendors. They would target locked houses and carry out thefts when they found an opportunity. Accused carried ₹25,000 reward each On April 17, 2026, police arrested both accused — Mohammad Sharik Jamal Ansari (38) and Reyaz Akram (27) — from Kashipuram Colony in the Seer Govardhanpur area. According to police, a reward of ₹25,000 each had been announced for their arrest. An official from the Bhelupur ACP office said that stolen jewellery worth about ₹40 lakh has been recovered from their possession. The recovered items include gold and silver necklaces, bangles, rings, earrings, and anklets.

stories.title: UP STF nabs main accused in Noida labour violence:NIT BTech graduate caught in Tamil Nadu, non-bailable warrant issued by court
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) has arrested Aditya Anand, the main accused in the Noida labour unrest case, from Tamil Nadu. He had been on the run for several days, while six teams of Noida Police were trying to trace him. Police said Anand, along with two others — Rupesh Rai and Manisha — allegedly instigated workers and played a key role in triggering the unrest. The three had created multiple WhatsApp groups on April 9 and 10 to mobilise workers, officials said. A case had been registered against Anand at the Phase-2 police station in Gautam Buddha Nagar district. A local court had also issued a non-bailable warrant (NBW) against him. According to investigators, the unrest was not spontaneous but planned in advance. During the probe, police also found indications of a possible international link. Officials said two social media handles on X (formerly Twitter) — @Proudindiannavi and @Mir_Ilyas_INC — were allegedly being operated from Pakistan and were active during the period of unrest. Further investigation in the case is underway. Noida violence accused held in Tamil Nadu after multi-state search Aditya Anand, who carried a ₹1 lakh reward, has been arrested from a railway station in Tiruchirappalli after a multi-state search operation. Police teams used technical surveillance and conducted raids in several states before tracking him down. Anand is a BTech graduate from National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur. He was present in Noida during the labour unrest. Police allege he created multiple WhatsApp groups through QR codes to mobilise workers and delivered provocative speeches to incite violence. Online network used to fuel unrest Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh said misleading and inflammatory content was circulated through social media accounts to disturb law and order in Gautam Buddh Nagar. These accounts were operated using VPNs to hide identities. Investigators said the network had been active for nearly three months. Some IP addresses have links to Pakistan. Authorities are now examining back-end data to trace the full extent of the alleged digital conspiracy. Key role in organising protests Probe agencies said Anand, along with Rupesh Rai and Manisha, played a key role in mobilising workers. The trio was active in Noida on March 31 and April 1. Between April 9 and 10, they allegedly created several WhatsApp groups and called on workers to protest, damage property and turn violent. On April 13, violence broke out across parts of Noida, with mobs pelting stones and setting vehicles on fire. So far, 63 accused have been arrested. Protests turned violent across industrial areas The unrest began on April 9, when factory workers protested over wage demands. With no resolution, workers took to the streets on April 13. Clashes broke out when police intervened. The protest, which began in Phase-2, spread to nearly 10 industrial sectors. In Sector 57, more than 30 factories and offices were vandalised. Companies in Sectors 40 and 60 were surrounded, while a factory gate in Sector 85 was broken. Roads were blocked in multiple sectors and near the DND Flyover. Security forces, including PAC and RAF, were deployed to control the situation. Further attempts at unrest were reported on April 14. Police crackdown and government action Police and paramilitary forces conducted flag marches, while CCTV and drones were used for surveillance. Around 200 workers were detained and cases were filed against about 60 people. Several factories were shut, while others shifted to work-from-home. The Government of Uttar Pradesh has formed a high-level committee to probe the incident. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said strict action would be taken against those behind the unrest. The state government also announced a wage hike of up to ₹3,000 for factory workers, effective from April 1.

stories.title: Stay on FIR order against Rahul Gandhi:Allahabad HC reviews its direction; says action without prior notice not legally appropriate
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court’s Lucknow bench has stayed its own earlier order directing registration of an FIR against Rahul Gandhi in a case related to alleged dual citizenship. The update was published on the court’s website on Saturday. The court said a hearing was held on April 17, where it asked the petitioner and lawyers for the Centre and state whether a notice should be issued to Rahul Gandhi. The lawyers said a notice was not necessary, following which the court initially ordered registration of an FIR. However, before the order was formally issued, Justice Subhash Vidyarthi reviewed the matter again. He noted a 2014 judgment of the High Court, which states that in cases seeking FIR registration, if a plea is dismissed, only a revision petition is maintainable — and the proposed accused must be given notice. Based on this, the court said it would not be appropriate to proceed without issuing notice to Rahul Gandhi. The next hearing has been scheduled for April 20. The petition was filed by S. Vignesh Shishir, a resident of Karnataka. He has made allegations against Rahul Gandhi under the Indian Justice Code, Official Secrets Act, Foreigners Act, and Passport Act. Following the development, the petitioner said he would approach the Chief Justice of India against the decision to withdraw the FIR order. Order to register FIR was given on April 17 The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court on Friday ordered the registration of an FIR against Rahul Gandhi in a case related to alleged dual citizenship. Justice Subhash Vidyarthi directed that the FIR be registered and the matter be handed over to the CBI. The petition was filed by Vignesh Shishir, a BJP worker from Karnataka. Earlier, on January 28, 2026, the MP-MLA court had dismissed his plea, stating that no new or concrete evidence regarding citizenship had been presented. While overturning the lower court’s order, the High Court observed that the magistrate did not need to comment on the truthfulness of the allegations at that stage. Centre submits ‘top secret’ files During the hearing, the court asked the Foreigners Division of the Home Ministry to submit all relevant documents. The Ministry presented the case-related files before the court. The petitioner claimed he had submitted documents indicating that Rahul Gandhi was listed as a voter in the United Kingdom and had records linked to participation in elections there. Case moved from Raebareli to Lucknow The complaint was initially filed in the MP-MLA court in Raebareli. On the petitioner’s request, the High Court transferred the case to Lucknow on December 17, 2025. After the Lucknow court dismissed the plea in January 2026, the petitioner approached the High Court, which first ordered the FIR and later stayed its own order. Similar plea dismissed earlier In 2019, the Supreme Court of India had dismissed a similar petition on Rahul Gandhi’s citizenship. Then Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi said that mentioning someone as a British citizen in company records does not automatically make them a British citizen. The bench had ruled that the petition had no merit and rejected the plea seeking action from the Home Ministry and disqualification of Rahul Gandhi from elections. Three cases against Rahul in Uttar Pradesh Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is currently facing three separate cases in Uttar Pradesh. Lost MP seat in Modi surname case Rahul Gandhi lost his Lok Sabha membership on March 24, 2023, after being convicted by a Gujarat court in the Modi surname defamation case. However, on August 4, 2023, the Supreme Court of India stayed his conviction. Following this, the Lok Sabha Secretariat restored his membership on August 7, 2023.

Codeine cough syrup mastermind’s father denied bail:Booked under PIT NDPS like NSA, action based on SIT report
stories.summary: Bhola Jaiswal, father of alleged codeine cough syrup mastermind Shubham Jaiswal, will not be eligible for bail for one year after being booked under the PIT NDPS Act. The action, considered equivalent to the National Security Act (NSA) in its preventive detention effect, was approved by the state government following a proposal from Sonbhadra police. Superintendent of Police Abhishek Verma said the move was based on findings of a Special Investigation Team (SIT), which identified Bhola Jaiswal as a habitual offender in the illegal codeine cough syrup trade. The approval was granted after a recommendation was sent to the government through Sonbhadra District Magistrate B.N.A. Singh. The order came into effect on April 15. Arrested while attempting to flee Bhola Jaiswal, a resident of Kayastha Tola in Prahlad Ghat, Varanasi, and owner of Shaili Traders, was arrested by Sonbhadra police on December 1, 2025, from Kolkata airport while allegedly trying to leave the country. He is currently lodged in Sonbhadra jail. With the PIT NDPS Act invoked, he will neither be able to apply for bail nor be granted bail for one year. Properties worth ₹36 crore attached Police said properties worth ₹36 crore linked to Bhola Jaiswal have already been attached. Officials added that the process is underway to convert these assets into government property under legal provisions. Smuggling through fake billing: SIT findings According to the SIT probe, Bhola Jaiswal was involved in smuggling codeine-based cough syrup using forged or manipulated bills through his firm, Shaili Traders. The investigation concluded that he was a repeat offender, prompting authorities to initiate preventive detention under PIT NDPS. SP Verma said a detailed dossier was prepared by the SIT and forwarded to the government, which granted approval for the stringent action.

stories.title: Akshaya Tritiya buzz in Gorakhpur:Gold and silver sales may rise by 20%, over 350 vehicles booked
stories.summary: Gorakhpur is seeing strong demand ahead of Akshaya Tritiya, with brisk bookings for gold, silver, cars and bikes. Traders expect jewellery sales to rise by about 20% compared to last year. Jewellers say customers have been booking in advance, helped by relatively lower gold prices. Sanjay Agarwal, Director of Parampara Gems and Jewels, said the market has been active for the past week and sales are likely to grow by around 20% this year. Auto sector sees strong bookings Automobile dealers also report high demand. Around 8–9 car dealerships in the city expect combined sales of over 200 cars on the day. Abhishek Agarwal, MD of Orbit Automobile, said his showroom alone will deliver more than 60 vehicles. Among cars, the Maruti Suzuki Invicto is expected to be the most expensive delivery, while the Maruti Suzuki Vitara is likely to see the highest number of deliveries. Bike demand rises, youth show interest Bike sales are also set to surge. Dealers estimate that more than 400 bikes could be sold across the city. Popular models include the Jawa Bobber, which has strong demand among young buyers, along with the Yamaha MT-15 and Yamaha R15. With around 25 bike agencies in the city, each is expected to sell 15–20 units on average. Many deliveries have already been scheduled for the festival day. Weddings add to festive demand The wedding season is also driving sales. More than 100 weddings are expected to take place in the city on Akshaya Tritiya. About 75% of marriage halls have already been booked, while some families are planning ceremonies at home. Overall, traders and dealers say the festival, along with the start of the wedding season, is boosting consumer spending across sectors.

stories.title: Kanpur gas shortage leaves residents waiting in long queues:Women wait with umbrellas in scorching heat; allege gas black marketing
stories.summary: Residents in Kanpur are facing a severe shortage of cooking gas, with long queues reported across several areas. Many people are standing in line for hours under the scorching sun, yet returning empty-handed due to irregular supply. The administration claims that home delivery services are in place, but residents say the system is not working effectively on the ground. According to them, they first have to queue up to book a cylinder and then wait again separately to receive it. People wait under sun, supply fails to arrive A large number of residents gathered at Bhagwat Indane Gas Service near JK Temple on Friday, hoping to collect their cylinders. Many were seen sitting outside with umbrellas, waiting for the delivery vehicle. However, the gas supply did not arrive for a long time, triggering anger among those waiting. People said they have been visiting the agency repeatedly but are still unable to get cylinders. Residents have urged the administration to fix the system quickly and ensure regular supply to ease their difficulties. ‘Booked in march, still no cylinder,’ say residents Sagar Goyal said he had booked a cylinder on March 25 and received the DAC number on March 26. “I stood in line the whole day, and my turn came around 4 pm. We were told the cylinder would be given on April 18. But now they say it won’t come today,” he said. He alleged that cylinders are being sold illegally in the black market. “Gas vehicles are going to other parts of the city, but not here. Now we are being told to come again on Monday,” he added. People queue from early morning, allege poor communication Another resident, Tribhuvan, said people have been coming to the agency for the past three days. “We were given April 18 as the delivery date. I have been standing here since 8 am, while some people started queuing from 6 am,” he said. He added that the agency should have informed people earlier if the supply was not coming. “If they knew the vehicle wouldn’t arrive today, they should have told us in advance,” he said.

stories.title: Bomb threat to Jhansi judge, security tightened:Letter warns of April 30 attack, alleges bias against community
stories.summary: In Jhansi, Special Judge (SC/ST Act) Aditya Chaturvedi received a bomb threat through a letter sent by post. The letter alleges that the judge has “wrongly punished members of a community” in several cases and warns of a bomb attack inside the court premises by April 30. The letter was received on April 16. The sender’s name was mentioned as Mohammad Saleem Mansuri. On April 17, a district court official informed the City SP in writing. Police registered a case the same night and began an investigation. Security has been increased at the court premises, as well as at the judge’s residence. Letter sent from post office inside court campus Police said preliminary findings indicate that the letter was posted from a post office located within the court premises. The envelope carried the stamp of that post office. Officials have also identified the time at which the letter was sent. CCTV footage from nearby areas is being examined to trace the sender. Police said efforts are underway to identify the accused at the earliest. Initial suspicion points to a possible mischief attempt. Judge’s security increased Assistant Superintendent of Police Ariba Noman said the threat appears to be an attempt to intimidate the judge. She said the matter is being taken seriously, a case has been registered, and an investigation is in progress. Security arrangements at the court and for the judge have been strengthened.

stories.title: Aparna Yadav protests over Woman's Reservation bill setback:Says, 'Oppn's face pretentious, Nari Shakti will crush them'; SP-Congress flag burnt in Lucknow
stories.summary: BJP leader and UP Women's Commission Vice President Aparna Yadav staged a protest late Friday night in front of the Assembly in Lucknow. Along with commission officials and supporters, she burned SP and Congress flags in the middle of the road and raised slogans over the Women's Reservation Bill being dropped in the Lok Sabha. Aparna said- We were going to celebrate in the morning. But, tonight proved to be dark. These people are like Duryodhana and Dushasana. That's why we are burning their flags. We are protesting because the Nari Shakti Adhiniyam Bill was not passed. The darkness will fade, the sun will rise, the lotus will bloom. She said that the opposition has said that this bill is for show, so we respond to them that all their faces are also for show. All opposition parties have been doing the same work. They never want daughters and daughters-in-law from common households to come out and reach the House. They only want to promote their own families. Nari Shakti will never forgive these people. Ugly face of opposition exposed Aparna said that if this bill had been passed, there would have been celebrations in the morning. For this, we were going to different districts of the state for different programs. We were fully confident that the bill would definitely be passed. We thank the Prime Minister again and again for exposing the ugly face of the opposition. She said that the PM made a lot of effort to get the Women's Empowerment Act passed. But, what has happened today is not right. This is a night that brings disgrace. In our country, where the slogan of Bharat Mata Ki Jai is raised. Women's power will not forgive them. They will crush them. Women protested in front of SP office Women also protested around 10 PM outside the Samajwadi Party office. Angered by the non-passage of the women's reservation bill, they raised slogans of "Akhilesh Yadav-Rahul Gandhi Murdabad". A member of the UP Women's Commission said that women's dreams were shattered due to the bill not being passed. Akhilesh is responsible for this. Meanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav wrote on X - BJP should have at least sent 12 women to the protest. Bill needed to be passed with two-thirds majority Actually, the government could not pass the 131st Constitutional Amendment Bill related to the Women's Reservation Bill in the Lok Sabha. It had a provision to increase the 543 seats of Parliament to 850. Voting took place after 21 hours of discussion on the bill in the Lok Sabha. 528 MPs present cast their votes. 298 votes in favor, 230 votes against. A two-thirds majority was needed to pass the bill. Know about Aparna Yadav

stories.title: Assistant Professor re-examination begins today amid tight security:Centres in six UP cities, including Varanasi; life imprisonment for those who cheat or aid cheating
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission is conducting a re-examination for Assistant Professor-51 starting today, April 18. This is being organized under strict surveillance. For this examination, which will be held over 2 days, a total of 48 examination centers have been set up in 6 cities, including Varanasi. The examination is being held in Varanasi, Prayagraj, Agra, Meerut, Lucknow, and Gorakhpur. In Varanasi, 8 examination centers have been established for this purpose. The Commission's Chairman and former DGP Dr. Prashant Kumar, has imposed special strictness regarding this examination. He has stated that if anyone is caught cheating or facilitating cheating in the examination, or attempting any kind of breach, they will be directly sentenced to life imprisonment. Monitoring being done from control room set up in the commission All rooms of the examination centers and all important sections have been equipped with CCTV. Its monitoring has been connected to the district control room and the commission's command and control room. Candidates arriving at the examination center will be allowed entry only after proper frisking. Prohibitory orders have been imposed around all examination centers. The District Magistrate, Senior Police Officers, and their monitoring teams have been instructed to continuously visit the examination centers. The district administration has deployed adequate force at the examination centers. Various security agencies are maintaining a vigilant watch to strictly monitor suspicious and anti-social elements. Use of any kind of electronic devices, mobile phones, etc., by candidates at examination centers will be prohibited. Vimal Kumar Vishwakarma, observer for Varanasi One member each has been designated as observer for each district and sent to the districts. Vimal Kumar Vishwakarma has been appointed as observer for Varanasi. He reached the district and also took into account the arrangements. Similarly, Dr. Krishna Chandra Verma in Gorakhpur, Dr. Harendra Kumar Rai in Prayagraj, Kirti Gautam in Agra, Prof. Radhakrishnan in Meerut, and Yogendra Nath Singh in Lucknow have been designated as observers. Don't pay attention to rumors: Chairman Commission Chairman Prashant Kumar has appealed to all examinees to reach the examination centers on time and strictly comply with the instructions written in the admit card. In accordance with government directives, all necessary arrangements have been ensured at the examination centers in their interest. Candidates should not fall prey to any rumors or misleading information. They should verify information on the Commission's website www.upessc.up.gov.in and 'X' handle @upesscprayagraj. Same examination being conducted again after one year Actually, the Uttar Pradesh Education Service Selection Commission had conducted a written examination on April 16 and 17, 2025, under Number-51 for 910 Assistant Professor posts in aided degree colleges. More than 82 thousand candidates had applied for the recruitment. However, immediately after the examination, complaints of large-scale fraud, cheating, and illegal extortion started surfacing. Candidates also continued to stage sit-in protests regarding this. Considering the seriousness of the case, the STF conducted a confidential investigation under the CM's direction. A major revelation was made in the investigation. After this, the STF arrested three members of the gang - Mahboob Ali, Baijnath Pal, and Vinay Pal, who were cheating candidates by preparing fake question papers.

stories.title: Yogi asks Mamata to vacate throne, questions Bengal leadership:Adds BJP rule will end 'love jihad' in state; 'Bulldozer Baba' slogans raised
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday said he had come to tell West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee to “vacate the throne” as the BJP would come to power in the state. He said a BJP “double-engine government” would stop what he described as “love jihad” and “land jihad”. He also accused the Trinamool Congress of supporting infiltrators. Remarks on women’s reservation Adityanath said the opposition does not want to give women their rights. Referring to Parliament, he alleged that Congress, Samajwadi Party and Left parties did not allow a proposal linked to 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha from 2029 to pass. He called it an insult to women. Criticism of TMC’s slogan He said TMC spoke of “Maa, Maati, Manush”, but questioned its stand on women’s reservation. He alleged that infiltrators are being settled on land and people are living in fear. Rally in Mathabhanga Adityanath reached West Bengal to campaign for BJP candidates and held his first rally in Mathabhanga. Slogans of “Bulldozer Baba zindabad” were raised as he came on stage. References to Bengal’s legacy He referred to figures such as Ramakrishna Paramahamsa, Rabindranath Tagore and Subhas Chandra Bose. He also mentioned Syama Prasad Mukherjee and said Prime Minister Narendra Modi fulfilled his vision by removing Article 370. Comparison with Uttar Pradesh He said the situation in Uttar Pradesh before 2017 was similar to Bengal, with riots and curfews. He claimed that now there are no riots or curfews in the state. Claims on law and order He said mafia properties in Uttar Pradesh were used to build houses for the poor. He added that similar changes would happen in Bengal if the BJP forms the government. Final appeal Adityanath urged voters to support the BJP, saying Bengal has a “final opportunity” for a double-engine government. He repeated his message asking Mamata Banerjee to step down, saying the BJP is coming to power.

stories.title: Hottest day of the season in UP, temperature hits 45.4°C:School timings changed; elephants being bathed repeatedly in zoo
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is witnessing intense heat, with temperatures crossing 45°C. On Friday, Banda recorded 45.4°C, the highest in the country. Since Saturday morning, most districts have been experiencing strong sunlight and hot winds. At Gorakhpur Zoo, elephants like ‘Ganga Prasad’ are being bathed repeatedly to provide relief from the heat. In Kaushambi, water has been arranged in the collectorate premises for monkeys, many of which were seen drinking and playing in it. In Varanasi, school timings up to Class 8 have been changed due to the heat. Classes will now run from 7:30 am to 1 pm. Children were seen heading to school with faces covered and carrying umbrellas. In 17 districts, including Prayagraj and Jhansi, maximum temperatures crossed 40°C. Last year, temperatures crossed 45°C in the last week of April (April 27), but this year the heatwave has arrived about 10 days earlier. However, the weather changed in western UP on Friday evening, with storms and rain in Noida, Ghaziabad, Meerut, and Muzaffarnagar, uprooting trees and electric poles in several places. In Moradabad’s Mundhapande area, a wall of a house collapsed during a late-night storm on Friday, killing a husband and wife who were sleeping in the courtyard. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Singh said temperatures may rise by 2–3°C over the next three days and could reach 47–48°C by the end of the month. A new western disturbance may become active, bringing cloud cover but no rain, increasing humidity, and creating heatwave-like conditions in some areas.

stories.title: Allahabad HC makes Basti SP stand for hours:Faces action over wrong affidavit and delays in murder case; officer apologises
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court made the Basti SP stand for four hours over police negligence in a murder case. The court reprimanded, saying that the person who is in charge of the district should be vigilant about the information given by his inspector or constable. After this, the SP apologized to the court. The court said on Thursday that a lenient view is being taken on the SP's apology. Instead of passing any order against him, he is directed to remain present in the court until the court rises. So that in the future, while filing affidavits before the High Court or any court, he exercises more caution. Actually, the entire matter is related to the murder of a young woman. In this, an affidavit with incorrect facts was filed in the court by the Basti police. Also, the report was not sent on time. The postmortem report also did not reveal the evidence that the police had included in their investigation. Now read the complete case The incident dates back to September 25, 2025. A young woman who had gone to the fields in the Walterganj police station area of Basti was murdered. The allegation was that the woman was attacked with a brick and a heavy object. After the woman's murder, poison was put in her mouth, but even the postmortem report did not find clear evidence of serious injury. The murder accusation was against Manjeet Kumar, along with 3 unknown persons. According to the family members, the accused were pressuring the woman for marriage. When she refused, this incident was carried out. The police had registered an FIR in this case after 17 days. Court angered over late submission of report The accused in the case had filed a bail petition in the High Court. During the hearing, the court requested para-wise comments from the police station. However, the police took considerable time to send the report. The court strongly objected to this. Station House Officer Walterganj Upendra Singh was also summoned. During the hearing, Station House Officer Upendra Singh and investigating Head Constable Manoj Yadav held the prosecution officer responsible for the delay. Following this, the court also summoned Prosecution Officer Rajiv Kumar. Subsequently, the court summoned SP Basti on April 7, 2026. Basti police's negligence came to light On April 16, 2026, both the SP Basti and the Prosecution Officer appeared personally in court. The court found negligence on the part of the Basti police in taking action in the murder case. The court expressed displeasure at the SP's working style and directed him to stand in court for the entire time. SP apologizes SP Yashvir Singh admitted his mistake and apologized unconditionally. After this, the court warned him to be careful in the future. Meanwhile, considering the merits of the case, the court granted bail to the accused Manjeet Kumar. The court also said that there is no eyewitness in the case. There is only the circumstance of being seen together for the last time. The postmortem report also does not have clear evidence of serious injury, which creates a situation of doubt. While granting conditional bail, the court directed the accused not to influence witnesses and to cooperate in the trial.

stories.title: 'Womb on rent':Girls give birth using sperm of unknown men in UP, fair-skinned, unmarried attract higher price
stories.summary: “Look, this girl has already given birth once by renting her womb. She is slim; earlier she took ₹10 lakh, now she is demanding ₹15 lakh. We have a big network, with 10 centres in Lucknow alone, where girls are made to conceive using (donor) semen. I currently have 10 women with me,” says an agent, who is also a doctor. This was stated by the operator of a private hospital in Uttar Pradesh, who is allegedly the kingpin of a womb-for-rent racket. The gang fixes the price for a woman to bear a child based on her age, physique, appearance and facial features. If she is considered attractive, the cost can go up to ₹15 lakh, while an average woman is paid around ₹5 lakh. The racket is reportedly operating across Uttar Pradesh. They have a network of several women, some of whom are unmarried. Their targets are couples who are unable to have children and for whom IVF has failed. Such couples are promised parenthood through surrogacy. These women conceive using the man’s semen and initially stay at home for 4-5 months. As the pregnancy becomes visible, they are shifted to centres run by the gang to avoid attention from relatives and neighbours. At these centres, the gang covers the woman’s food, accommodation and medical expenses. After 9 months, the baby is delivered and handed over to the couple. Despite strict laws governing surrogacy, Dainik Bhaskar conducted an investigation to expose this illegal racket operating in Uttar Pradesh. Read the complete expos Sources allege that Afzal Ansari, owner of Sahara Welcare Hospital near Lucknow, is running an illegal surrogacy racket. After multiple attempts, he agreed to meet and explained the process. He told reporters that surrogacy costs ₹7–10 lakh, involving IVF with no physical contact. He warned that failed embryo formation could lead to financial loss. He also claimed that babies can be arranged directly for ₹5–6 lakh. Afzal cited cases where couples, after failed surrogacy attempts, chose to obtain a child directly, saying it avoids further risk and expense. In the very first meeting with Afzal, it became clear that he was running a racket of selling wombs. He also sells babies. Where do the threads of this business extend to? To understand this, we asked him some direct questions. 'The woman is in Bihar, delivery will be done there' Reporter: Where will the surrogacy process take place? Afzal: Everything will happen in Bihar, 400 kilometres away from Lucknow. Reporter: How will the meeting with the surrogate woman happen? Afzal: When you are spending so much money, we will arrange a meeting too. First, we will arrange a meeting, then you people can meet in between as well. Reporter: What will be the woman's age? Where will she stay? Afzal: She will be around 25-26 years old. We will show you her room and everything, and she will stay separately on rent. Reporter: Will we have to pay her separately? Afzal: No, don't give money, you can give rations. Reporter: So, how much expense should we consider? Will everything be done within ₹10 lakh? Afzal: Yes... In Lucknow, there was a poor couple; we got them a 1-day-old girl for just ₹2 lakh. Absolutely fair-complexioned. We also gave a boy to another couple for ₹6 lakh. Reporter: Then why don't you rent the womb of a UP girl? Afzal: There is a lot of politics here, that's why we take Bihar girls. When you need to see, we will bring her to Lucknow. Reporter: Will there be any agreement? Between you and the girl... Afzal: There is no agreement; papers don't work in this line, everything is done verbally. Reporter: How will the payment be made? Where will the delivery happen? Afzal: First, 50% payment has to be given in advance. We'll arrange a meeting with the girl. Then the remaining payment has to be given later. We do it in Bihar itself; it will be better there. Hospital owner Afzal Ansari also said that he deliberately runs the network by changing states, so that he can avoid surveillance. A few days later, our team met Afzal with a couple of female reporters, so that he would be fully convinced that we need a child. This time, when Afzal trusted us, he spoke openly about the entire racket. 'Surrogate woman stays 5 months at her home, then 4 months in our arrangement' Afzal: (Looking at the female reporter) You have brought Madam, that's good. Reporter: Madam has to go back to Bengaluru, she has an evening flight. Afzal: If I call the surrogate woman, it will take 4-5 hours. Reporter: No problem, you call her. Afzal: Then let's call her at 9 PM tonight. Reporter: Won't the woman's husband find out when the baby is born? Afzal: The deal is made with the husband, and payment is also made to him. The woman tells relatives that she is working away from home. Female Reporter: Do you talk to both husband and wife? Afzal: Yes, we talk to both. Reporter: If we give the woman ₹500-1,000 separately, there won't be any problem, right? Afzal: You can give, but not too much. We provide her accommodation, food, treatment, ultrasound, medicine - everything. The woman stays at her home or in our arrangement for 5 months. If needed, we provide a room, and we keep them for 9 to 12 months. Afzal had first told us that the woman was from Bihar. But when we reached as a couple, he told us that the woman was from Gorakhpur. She will come from there, because now he has gained trust in us. 'The woman is from Gorakhpur, we will arrange delivery in Lucknow' Reporter: Where will the woman come from? Afzal: From Gorakhpur. Actually, the surrogate mother and her husband lied to their family and society that they had a baby, but it died. Look, they do this to save themselves. The woman stays at home for 5 months, but in the last 4 months, she has to take a separate room. That's where most of the expense occurs. We also take more care during that time, when she stays at home, we also send money for expenses. Reporter: Where will the delivery take place? Afzal: We have our own centres, from Lucknow to Delhi, Bengaluru, Mumbai, Bihar, and Gorakhpur. From Afzal's statements, it became clear that his racket is spread across Delhi, Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Bihar. After this, at 9 PM, we met Afzal again with a female reporter. This time, the woman offering her womb for rent was also caught on our hidden camera. Reporter: Where is the woman? Afzal: She's coming, she'll be here in the room in 5 minutes. As soon as you people left my office this morning, I got worried about calling the woman. But, we have a complete system in place. That's why the woman comes easily. You won't believe it, a woman can earn up to ₹5 lakh in 9 months. Reporter: Oh, that happens. Afzal: If I get a fever, I can manage it, but for a surrogate woman, arrangements have to be made immediately; there's concern about the client. (After about 20 minutes, the surrogate woman was brought before us.) Reporter: What is your name? There won't be any problem, will there? Surrogate Woman: My name is Sita. There will be no difficulty. Reporter: Is there any problem at home? How many children do you have? Surrogate Woman: No...one child died, I have one boy and one girl. Reporter: Have you done this before? There won't be any problem later, right? Surrogate Woman: No, there will be no problem. I am doing this for the first time. Reporter: Where will you stay during this period? Afzal: (interrupting) I will arrange for this, you don't worry. She will stay at her home for a few months, then we will call her. Reporter: Will you keep her in Lucknow itself? Afzal: Yes, if she stays nearby, it will be convenient for you too. Reporter: Later, won't she refuse to give the baby? Surrogate Woman: That won't happen. Afzal: Don't worry, I give you my word. Reporter: What will you tell your husband? Surrogate Woman: Will tell him clearly, he (husband) has already left me. Afzal: She is from a village. Has two healthy children. Don't ask too many questions. We have already discussed everything. Reporter: Do I need to give some token money? Afzal: Yes, please give it. Afzal initially quoted ₹10 lakh for surrogacy but raised it to ₹12 lakh after sensing the couple could pay more. ‘It will cost ₹12 lakh, ₹5–6 lakh in advance’ Reporter: How will payment be made? Afzal: In cash. ₹10 lakh for arrangement, ₹2 lakh for treatment. Reporter: So ₹12 lakh? Afzal: Yes. ₹5–6 lakh advance, rest later. Reporter: Do we pay the woman separately? Afzal: No, we give her a credit card. After the work, it’s blocked. The reporter later met surrogate Sita and gave her ₹500 on a hidden camera. ‘Don’t worry, I won’t think it’s someone else’s child’ Female Reporter: You won’t have a problem? Sita: No. I already have two children. Female Reporter: Where are you from? Sita: Brother must have told you. Afzal also offered a direct deal: a 1–2-day-old boy for ₹5–6 lakh, a girl for ₹2 lakh. He further claimed an unmarried woman in his network has given birth to five children since 2018. Now know the rules of surrogacy Only relatives can become surrogate mothers; taking money is a crime After understanding the surrogacy racket, our team spoke with Lucknow High Court Senior Advocate Arvind Verma about what rules and laws exist in the country. Question: What are the rules regarding surrogate mothers in the country? Answer: Under the Surrogacy Regulation Act 2021, only altruistic surrogacy is permitted in India, while commercial surrogacy is prohibited. According to the rules, the needy couple must have the woman aged between 25 and 50 years and the man aged between 26 and 55 years. They should not have any living child. The surrogate mother can only be a close relative. Paying her for this work is illegal. Question: What are the rules for clinics conducting surrogacy? Answer: Clinics conducting surrogacy must have a certificate and NOC from the District Medical Board. Violating these rules is a non-bailable offence, which can result in imprisonment of 5 to 10 years and a fine of ₹10 to 25 lakh.

stories.title: Firozabad Tehsildar accuses DM of harassment, corruption:Alleges iPhone and iWatch demand, salary withheld for 8 months, seeks justice from CM Yogi
stories.summary: Tundla Tehsildar Rakhi Sharma in Firozabad has levelled serious allegations against District Magistrate Ramesh Ranjan. Addressing a press conference at her office in the tehsil premises on Friday, she accused the DM of taking an iPhone and an iWatch worth ₹1.75 lakh and subjecting her to harassment. The Tehsildar stated that an inquiry was deliberately initiated against her. Exploitation was done in the name of ending it. She was made to sit in the office for hours. 8 months' salary was also withheld, which was released after approaching the High Court. She has demanded an investigation into the matter from Chief Minister Yogi. Tundla Tehsil's Tehsildar Rakhi Sharma released a video on Thursday late evening. In it, she appealed to the CM for justice. She said that District Magistrate Ramesh Ranjan Sir and some of his clerks have been harassing me for 9 months for corruption. There is one OSD, Shailendra Sharma, one Peshkar, and one CRA. These people have a group. An application came to my tehsil 9 months ago in July. It had allegations of corruption against these three clerks. I had complained about this to the DM, sir. Demand for iWatch and mobile phone DM sir and I had asked them to resolve it, but instead, these people came after me. These people misguided the DM, sir, and my salary was withheld for 8 months. After that, without hearing my side, I was given a one-sided adverse entry. Even this did not satisfy them, so they started making demands. Sometimes they would ask for an Apple iWatch, sometimes an iPhone. The iPhone that I gave, DM sir, is still using the same one; this should be investigated. I have the bill and other details of this. Read the audio conversation between Tehsildar and DM's OSD... OSD- The payment has to be sent directly to the company's account. It should not be done to him. It will reach wherever you are standing. Tehsildar- I am sending the driver. He drives very fast, and will reach in 20 minutes. I have called him here; he is standing outside. OSD- Are you sending your person? Tehsildar- Yes, I am sending my person. Because, even if that person comes from Agra, it will take him 20 to 25 minutes. From here, it will also take 20 to 25 minutes. OSD- Will reach comfortably in 20 to 25 minutes. Tehsildar- Will reach. Tell that boy to stand at the store, don't close the store. My boy will reach there in half an hour. Tehsildar- I'll also get the mobile from the driver. OSD- Yes, tell him to get the tempered glass installed and bring it. Tehsildar- If you say, I'll send the mobile in the morning, or should I send it tonight itself? OSD- Send it now, no problem. After this, the phone gets disconnected. Store kept open till late night for iPhone On the night of November 4, 2025, a showroom in Agra was kept open specially till late at night. The demand was made through OSD. I was forced repeatedly, even though I was not receiving my salary. Still, I somehow managed to arrange and buy the phone. Even after giving the phone, they wanted me to go there repeatedly, plead, and beg. There are some things I don't want to say, but they have some moral and immoral orders, which I should fulfill. What was possible, I did; what was not possible, I didn't do. Went to High Court when salary didn't come After this, I kept waiting for the salary to come now, but it didn't. Frustratedly, I went to the High Court and filed a writ. I filed the writ on February 26. When Sir found out on February 27, the treasury was opened at night, and my salary was sent. The SDM sir and SDM madam of my district, who are attached to the Collectorate, and a private individual were called. Apart from this, OSD Shailendra, through whom all work is done. The iPhone and iWatch were also given to him. In the presence of all four of them, I was called to the camp house. I was kept captive there for 2 hours. Hope from CM Yogi, will get justice I was forced to withdraw my petition. They have been upset about this till today. Several investigations are being conducted against me. After this, videos are being made viral by some media persons. I had filed a complaint against them on March 25, but no action has been taken till date. In a video message addressed to the Chief Minister, she said that such misconduct was being done with a female magistrate and a PCS officer in his state. “My job comes later, my dignity comes first. Sir, I expect you to ensure that I get justice,” she said. Posted in Tundla Tehsil since 2024 Originally a resident of Agra, Rakhi Sharma has been working as Tehsildar in Tundla Tehsil since September 4, 2024. Her salary was withheld for 8 months from August 2025. In February, she filed a petition in the High Court regarding non-payment of salary. The Tehsildar also alleged irregularities and distribution of government land worth crores of rupees by the babus of the district. She said that government lands have been wrongly distributed through collusion of some babus and officers. If this matter is investigated impartially, a major land scam could come to light. Also raised questions about transfer The Tehsildar also raised questions about his transfer. He stated that his transfer has been made from Tundla to Shikohabad, but he has not yet received the official letter. Despite this, another Tehsildar has been sent in his place. Employee Union comes out in protest The Uttar Pradesh Ministerial Collectorate Employees Union, Firozabad, has sent a letter to the Commissioner of Agra Division demanding legal action against the Tehsildar. In the letter sent by District Minister Sumit Kumar and President Pradeep Sharma of the union, it was stated that Rakhi Sharma has made serious allegations of land-related disputes and corruption against Collectorate Administrative Officer Rajendra Khanna, DLRC Daujiram, and DM's OSD Shailendra Sharma. These allegations are completely baseless.

stories.title: Asha Bhosle’s granddaughter reveals her final wish:Immerses ashes with tearful eyes in Kashi; says, 'Grandmother will return'
stories.summary: Bollywood playback singer Asha Bhosle's son Anand Bhosle and granddaughter Zanai reached Varanasi on Monday. Both boarded a boat from Assi Ghat. They immersed Asha Bhosle's ashes after reaching the middle of the Ganges. Zanai became emotional during the immersion of ashes. Tears started flowing from her eyes. Zanai said, “Grandmother had expressed her wish to immerse her ashes in Kashi before her death.” It may be noted that Asha Bhosle passed away on April 12 in Mumbai. Son said, ‘Mother had an unbreakable bond with Lord Shiva’ Son Anand Bhosle said, "Mother came to Kashi only once in her life, but she had an unbreakable bond with Lord Shiva. To fulfill her last wish, we have come here today with the ashes. We have also performed her pind daan (ritual offering). Earlier, Pindra MLA Awdhesh Singh had received the family members at Babatpur Airport at 9:30 AM. After the immersion of ashes, Anand Bhosle and daughter Janai rested at Taj Hotel. Then they left for Mumbai from here at 4 PM. Granddaughter made an emotional post on social media After Asha Bhosle's demise, Zanai Bhosle shared an emotional post on social media. She described her grandmother as her best friend and an important part of her life. Zanai wrote that now she doesn't understand with whom she will have morning tea or share jokes. She wrote that she believes her grandmother will always be with her and will return one day to embrace her again. She said that Asha Bhosle was not just a great artist, but for her, she was the identity of life and happiness. Read unheard stories related to Asha Bhosle's life Eloped and got married at the age of 16, relationship with sister deteriorated Asha Bhosle fell in love with her elder sister Lata's secretary Ganapat Rao Bhosle at just 16 years of age. Ganapat Rao was 15 years older. Asha knew that the family would not accept this relationship, so at the age of 16, she ran away from home and married Ganapat Rao. This decision brought her more troubles than happiness. After marriage, she did not receive good treatment from her husband and in-laws. Time passed and the bitterness in the relationship also increased. This relationship filled with suspicion and tension gave up after just a few years. Ganapat Rao threw her out of the house. At that time, Asha was with two children and was about to become a mother of a third child. Out of compulsion, she had to return to her maternal home. In the year 1960, both separated. RD Burman's mother had said, if you want to marry Asha, you will have to go over my dead body After divorcing Ganpat Rao, RD Burman came into Asha Bhosle's life as a companion. The two met in 1966 when they were working together in Teesri Manzil. Both lent their voices to O Haseena Zulfon Wali... and O Mere Sona Re Sona Re. RD Burman wanted to do something different from his father SD Burman's legacy. While bringing the trend of jazz and cabaret, he found support in Asha Bhosle's voice. Both created songs like Piya Tu Ab To Aaja... and Dum Maro Dum..., which led to Asha Bhosle being called the Cabaret Queen. The professional relationship soon became a reason for growing closeness. Pancham Da was 6 years younger than Asha. He had divorced his first wife Rita in 1971. His marriage was mired in controversies. Due to increasing domestic disputes, he had left home and started living in a hotel. When he decided to marry Asha 9 years later, the family turned against him. His mother flatly refused. RD Burman's mother was so upset with their relationship that she clearly stated that as long as she was alive, the two could not get married, and if they wanted to go through with this marriage, Asha would have to enter the house by stepping over her mother's dead body. Hearing this, RD Burman left without saying anything. He wanted to get married, but due to his mother's displeasure, it was not possible. After a few years, RD Burman's mother became very ill and stopped recognizing anyone. After this, RD Burman and Asha got married in 1980. 14 years after marriage, RD Burman passed away in 1994. Asha was alone once again. Before RD's death, his financial condition was not good, due to which Asha and he used to live separately.

stories.title: Father enraged by daughter’s affair strangles her in car:Burns face with acid, and dumps body in Barabanki
stories.summary: A case of honor killing has come to light in Lucknow. A father, along with his friend, strangled his minor daughter to death. To hide her identity, the accused poured acid on the teenager's face. After the crime, the body was dumped by the roadside on Kursi Road in Barabanki. To conceal the incident, the father fabricated a false story about his daughter going missing. He also filed a complaint on the online public grievance portal (IGRS). However, the case appeared suspicious during police investigation, following which the father and his friend were arrested on Sunday. During interrogation, both confessed to their crime. The accused father stated that his daughter used to talk to several boys. In 2025, she had also eloped from home with a boy. He was angry about this matter. This incident is from Dhawa area under Chinhat police station jurisdiction. The deceased teenager has been identified as 16-year-old Vandana Chaubey. Now read the sequence of events... DCP East Dr. Diksha Sharma said- On April 16, Vijay Kumar Chaubey (34), a resident of Dhawa, Chinhat, had lodged a complaint on IGRS about his 16-year-old daughter Vandana going missing. Based on the complaint, Chinhat police reached his house on April 18, but Vijay Kumar was not found at home. Upon inquiring in the neighborhood, it was found that he himself had taken his daughter along with him. Police tried to contact Vijay Kumar over phone, but his number was switched off. Investigation revealed that Vandana had eloped with a boy in 2025. On this angle, the police reached the boy's house, he was found at home. He told that on April 13, he had spoken to Vandana on the phone. Vandana had said that she was going for exorcism with her father and he should not call her. After this, there was no contact with him. From here, the police's suspicion on the father deepened. Surveillance was taken help of. On April 19, Vijay Kumar's location was found at his in-laws' place in Gonda. The police caught him from there the same day. During interrogation, Vijay Kumar confessed to killing his daughter along with his friend Abdul Mannan (45). After this, the police also arrested Abdul Mannan. Read the father's confession… During interrogation, the accused father Vijay Kumar Chaubey revealed - his daughter Vandana Chaubey used to talk to several boys. In the year 2025, she had run away from home with a boy. A case was also registered in this matter at Chinhat police station. After about 15 days, the police recovered her and handed her over to the family. Even after this, Vandana was in constant contact with that boy. Angered by this, the father plotted the murder. On April 13, Vijay Kumar, along with his friend Abdul Mannan, rented a car. He took his daughter to Barabanki on the pretext of exorcism. On the way, he stopped at a dhaba at night. The next day, on April 14, he took Vandana in the car to near Sharda Canal, Kursi Road in the Baddupur area of Barabanki. He murdered his daughter, who was sleeping in the car, by strangulating her. Vandana resisted, but Vijay Kumar and his friend Mannan kept pressing her throat until she died. After the murder, they tried to throw the body in the canal, but seeing people moving around, the accused got scared. After this, to destroy identification, they burned Vandana's face with acid and threw the body by the roadside and fled. Body was found in Barabanki, could not be identified DCP East Dr. Diksha Sharma said - After accused Vijay Kumar Chaubey confessed to the crime, Barabanki police was contacted. Vandana's photograph was sent to them. Barabanki police confirmed that on April 15, a girl's body was found near Sharda canal at Baddupur, Kursi Road. Attempts were made to identify the body, but were unsuccessful. After that, after waiting for three days, a postmortem was conducted as unidentified and the last rites were performed. Dr. Diksha Sharma said that now Chinhat police station and Barabanki police are taking the postmortem report and other evidence to proceed with further legal action.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Rampur court upholds 7-year sentence for Azam Khan son Abdullah; Munir calls peace talks 'tough' if Hormuz blockade continues and more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Munir tells Trump talks with Iran will be tough if Hormuz blockade continues US President Donald Trump and the Pakistani Army chief Asim Munir had a telephonic conversation on Monday. Asim Munir told Trump that if the ban on Hormuz continues, the talks with Iran will not be able to move forward. 2. Yogi cabinet expansion within 20 days, before 10 May: Focus on Brahmin, Dalit and women representation The Yogi Adityanath government plans to complete its cabinet expansion by May 10. Meanwhile, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is restructuring the state organization as part of preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. 3. Rampur court upholds 7-year sentence: Azam Khan, son Abdullah convicted in PAN card case filed by BJP leader SP leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam have been sentenced to seven years each. The Rampur court delivered this verdict in two separate cases related to PAN card fraud. Earlier, the MP-MLA court had also sentenced both to seven years. Azam and his son had appealed against this in the Sessions Court. 4. Mallikarjun Kharge calls PM Modi ‘jhuton ka sardar’ Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said in Cooch Behar, West Bengal, that Narendra Modi is the “jhuton ka sardar” and that he lies to win elections. 5. Mother performs last rites of twin daughters alone: Father arrested after confessing brutal murder at home A father in Kanpur has been arrested for brutally killing his 11-year-old twin daughters by slitting their throats. The accused, Shashi Ranjan Mishra, is now behind bars after the horrific incident that took place in Kidaiv Nagar. 6. MBBS students severely beat 'mentally ill' patient: Gorakhpur’s BRD Medical College student alleges objectionable remark on attire by patient At BRD Medical College in Gorakhpur, MBBS students allegedly beat up a 'mentally ill' patient. The patient is said to have come out of his ward and reached near Sarojini Hostel. There, he reportedly made a comment on the clothing of a student passing by. 7. 21 dead as bus falls into gorge in JK's Udhampur A bus fell about 100 feet off the road on Monday morning in JK's Udhampur region. 21 people were killed in the accident, while more than 29 passengers were injured. 8. UP govt transfers 40 IAS officers, 15 DMs: Shifts Kinjal Singh to education dept after face-off with minister The Yogi Adityanath-led Uttar Pradesh government carried out a major administrative reshuffle late Sunday night, transferring 40 IAS officers, including 12 women officers, and changing postings across several key departments and districts. The exercise, finalized after prolonged internal deliberations within the state administration, also involved a large-scale reshuffle of District Magistrates (DMs) across 15 districts. Officials said the move aligns with administrative rotation norms and preparations ahead of future electoral requirements. 9. Yogi government eases rules for farmers: Wheat sale allowed at govt centres without registration requirement in UP The Yogi government has given major relief to wheat farmers in Uttar Pradesh. Farmers will now be able to sell their wheat produce at government procurement centres without a farmer registry. 10. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi gets emotional, KKR staff consoles teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi turned emotional after Rajasthan Royals’s narrow loss to Kolkata Knight Riders in IPL 2026, with a consoling gesture from KKR staff going viral. Meanwhile, Varun Chakaravarthy revealed players cried after KKR’s first win, highlighting intense emotions in both camps.
