stories.title: Lucknow wedding turns tragic after fire:Bride fails to reach in-laws, groom arrives without procession; four stories of loss
stories.summary: We were preparing for the wedding. The nephew's baraat (groom's procession) was about to leave in an hour. Guests had arrived. Preparations were underway to adorn the groom. He was being applied ubtan (a traditional paste). The women of the house were singing songs. Suddenly, screams erupted. Someone shouted that there was a fire in the settlement. Saying this, Rani of Lucknow's voice choked. Tears welled up in her eyes. She had come to attend her nephew Manish's wedding. At the time when 250 huts caught fire in Vikas Nagar, the baraat was supposed to leave from there an hour later, but the fire burned everything to ashes. However, the family members took the baraat. The wedding took place, but due to the lack of a home, the bride's farewell could not happen. To understand the scene after the fire in Vikas Nagar, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached the ground. Here, they learned about the pain of the affected families. Read the report See 3 pictures of helplessness Fire guts wedding preparations, family devastated The groom’s aunt Rani, said the house was full of celebration, with the wedding procession set to leave in an hour when the fire broke out. As cylinders started exploding, everyone ran to save their lives. The groom’s sherwani, clothes, and the bride’s wedding dress and jewellery were destroyed. The wedding home turned into a scene of mourning, with people of all ages crying. Over 100 guests from different places also fled for safety. The family had bought a new saree with great hopes for the wedding, only that one remains. Rani said her sister, who works as a domestic helper, had borrowed ₹1.5 lakh for her son’s wedding and is now shattered. She appealed to the government for help. While the house was burning, Manish’s wedding procession had left, and his marriage with Madhu took place four hours later in Pani village, Indiranagar. Home destroyed before their eyes, Nandini kept sobbing Nandini was sitting 50 meters away from where the fire broke out. She was sobbing with tears in her eyes. We tried to talk to her. Sitting silently, Nandini said that this scene is very terrifying for her. Our childhood was spent here, this is the first time I've seen such a fire.Everything we had burned in this fire, we only managed to save our lives. When the accident happened, only my parents were at home. My sister and I had gone to work. That's where we got the information that our house was on fire, we rushed back and were stunned by the scene here. Fire destroys savings Nandini said the fire ruined their family's TV, fridge, and all their belongings were burnt. The family had saved ₹2.5 lakh through labor work for her wedding and made some jewelry, but both the cash and jewelry were destroyed in the blaze. She said the money was saved through sweeping and mopping work. All important documents were also burnt, including the papers of a car bought last Dhanteras. She appealed to the government for help, saying nothing is left except the clothes they were wearing. Fire leaves family missing An unconscious Shamsunnisha was being supported by a girl as she cried and beat her chest, saying everything they had was destroyed in the fire. She said they had married their daughter nine months ago, but even two hours after the blaze, there was no trace of her son and daughter-in-law. She added the family had been living there for 17 years and had no idea how the fire suddenly broke out. After her husband’s death, she survived by doing sweeping and mopping work, and her son and daughter-in-law were her only support. Now they are missing, and she says nothing is left. 250 homes destroyed A massive fire broke out in Vikas Nagar, Lucknow, on Wednesday evening. After the fire started, the sound of gas cylinders, refrigerators, and AC compressors exploding echoed all around. More than 40 cylinders exploded due to the fire. Over 250 shanties were burnt to ashes. Flames were visible up to 10 kilometers away. After the fire broke out, 20 fire brigade vehicles brought the fire under control after a struggle of about 7 hours. All the belongings of the people were burnt to ashes. Those whose shanties were burnt kept crying and wailing. Late at night, people were sent to temporary night shelters.

stories.title: Fire guts 250 huts in Lucknow’s Vikasnagar:Children search for toys in debris, women break down after devastation
stories.summary: An evening that began like any other in Vikasnagar turned chaotic on April 15 as a fire tore through a cluster of huts in Lucknow, triggering panic and desperate calls for help. Residents said the crackle of flames quickly drowned out the usual sounds of daily life, before a stunned silence settled over the area. Day after, survivors sift through ashes By morning, the extent of the damage became clear. Children searched the charred remains for toys, while adults looked for documents, cash and other essentials. Entire households were reduced to debris, leaving families with little to salvage. Losses both material and personal Among the survivors, grief was visible. A father broke down after finding his child’s burnt schoolbooks. Nearby, a woman wept over belongings she had saved for years. Officials said around 250 huts were destroyed, displacing several families. Tap on the photo above to watch the video of the aftermath.

stories.title: PM Modi calls Akhilesh 'friend' in Parliament:Shah says 'no need to fear'; sharp exchange fuels political buzz
stories.summary: The central government on Thursday introduced amendment bills related to the Women’s Reservation framework during a special session of Parliament, triggering a series of political exchanges inside the House. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while addressing members, referred to Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav as his “friend”. In response, Yadav smiled and folded his hands, drawing attention from members across party lines. Akhilesh–Shah exchange draws attention A debate between Yadav and Union Home Minister Amit Shah added intensity to the proceedings, with both leaders raising points over the implications and timing of the proposed amendments. Meanwhile, Union Minister Smriti Irani also became a subject of discussion during the session, despite not being a member of either House of Parliament at present. Political messaging dominates proceedings The session reflected not only legislative developments but also political signalling, with leaders using the platform to underline their respective positions on women’s representation and electoral strategy. Watch the video of the Parliament debate for full details.

stories.title: Car mows down 3 women sitting on divider in Hapur:Victims were waiting for bus, two critically injured
stories.summary: A speeding car ran over people sitting on a road divider in Hapur on Thursday evening, killing three women and injuring two others. The accident took place in the Hafizpur police station area when the car was travelling from Hapur towards Bulandshahr. Police said the driver lost control near Yadav Dhaba in Murshidpur village, after which the vehicle climbed onto the divider. Victims were waiting for transport Several people were sitting on the divider waiting for a bus or auto when the car hit them. Sitara (52), Sharda (52), and Saroj Sharma (60), all residents of Brijnatpur, died on the spot. Ruby (25) and her six-year-old son Lavish were seriously injured and taken to hospital. Driver detained, vehicle seized The car (UP15 CJ 6315) was being driven by Naresh, a resident of Meerut. He was taken into custody. Police removed the damaged vehicle and restored traffic. Bodies of the deceased have been sent for post-mortem. Officials visit spot, probe underway District Magistrate Abhishek Pandey and Superintendent of Police KG Singh inspected the site. ASP Vineet Bhatnagar said the car hit women sitting on the divider after going out of control. He confirmed three deaths and said further legal action is underway. Family account of incident According to Manoj, son of Sharda, the family was waiting by the roadside to travel to Narena village in Dhaulana. Sharda had accompanied her daughter Ruby. The accident occurred while they were waiting for transport.

90-year-old mother arrested for laundering son’s drug money in South Korea
stories.summary: A 90-year-old South Korean woman was sentenced for laundering hundreds of millions of won linked to her son's drug trafficking. She transferred funds at his direction while he was imprisoned abroad, acting as an intermediary. The court found her aware of the illicit nature of the money, contributing to the spread of narcotics.

stories.title: Meet Yvon Chouinard: The billionaire who gave away his $3 billion company to save the planet
stories.summary: Patagonia founder Yvon Chouinard made a groundbreaking move, gifting his $3 billion company to environmental causes. Instead of personal profit, the company's earnings now fund climate action and conservation. This unique structure, separating control from financial benefit, ensures Patagonia's profits directly support the planet's health, sparking global debate on purpose-driven business.
